title: Survival Skills Academy
description: Essential outdoor, emergency, and life skills to keep you safe and self-reliant in any situation.

personal_safety.name: Stranger Awareness
learning_objectives: Identify safe adults
Know what to do if approached by a stranger
Understand personal boundaries
key_steps: Learn the 'safe adult' circle (family, known teachers)
Recognise warning signs: adult asking for help, offering gifts
Practise saying 'No, I'm going to find a trusted adult'
Know your full name, parent's name, and phone number
practice_activities: Role-play with a parent: practise saying no and walking away
Memorise emergency contact number

quiz.q: What should you do if a stranger offers you a gift?
quiz.a: Say no and find a trusted adult immediately

quiz.q: Who is in your 'safe adults' circle?
quiz.a: Parents, known family members, and school staff

personal_safety.important_note: This lesson is for awareness and safety — always practise with a trusted adult at home.

personal_safety.name: Lost Child Procedures
learning_objectives: Know what to do when lost in a public place
Identify safe places to go
Stay calm and find help
key_steps: STOP: stay where you are if safe
Look for a uniformed worker (police, shop assistant)
Go to a customer service desk in a shop
Call out to a mum or dad with children nearby
Never leave with a stranger even if they say your parents sent them
practice_activities: Practise with a parent: what would you do if separated in a shopping centre?
Memorise your parent's phone number

quiz.q: What is the first thing to do if you get lost?
quiz.a: Stop and stay where you are if it is safe

quiz.q: Who is a safe person to ask for help when lost in a shop?
quiz.a: A uniformed shop worker or customer service staff

personal_safety.important_note: Always practise this scenario with a parent or guardian.

personal_safety.name: Online Safety Basics
learning_objectives: Identify safe and unsafe online behaviour
Know not to share personal information
Report uncomfortable content to a trusted adult
key_steps: Never share: full name, address, school, or phone number online
Use privacy settings on apps
If someone online makes you uncomfortable, tell an adult
Recognise phishing attempts and fake messages
Block and report — do not engage with trolls
practice_activities: Review privacy settings on a device with a parent
Discuss: what information is safe to share online and what is not

quiz.q: Name one thing you should never share online.
quiz.a: Home address, school name, phone number, or full name

quiz.q: What should you do if someone online makes you uncomfortable?
quiz.a: Tell a trusted adult immediately

personal_safety.important_note: Online safety rules apply to everyone, including friends and classmates.

personal_safety.name: Body Safety and Personal Boundaries
learning_objectives: Understand the concept of personal boundaries
Know the correct terms for body parts
Know how to say no and report unsafe touch
key_steps: Understand: your body belongs to you
Safe vs unsafe touch: medical, accidental vs uncomfortable
Practise saying 'No, stop, I will tell'
Always tell a trusted adult if something feels wrong
practice_activities: Role-play boundary scenarios with a parent
Practise the phrases: 'No', 'Stop', 'I will tell'

quiz.q: What should you do if a touch feels uncomfortable?
quiz.a: Say no, get away, and tell a trusted adult

quiz.q: Whose body belongs to you?
quiz.a: Your own body belongs to you

personal_safety.important_note: This lesson should be guided and discussed by a parent or guardian.

personal_safety.name: Safe Use of the Internet and Social Media
learning_objectives: Understand digital footprint
Recognise cyberbullying and how to respond
Protect passwords and accounts
key_steps: A digital footprint is everything you post online — it can be permanent
Use strong passwords (12+ characters, mix of types)
Cyberbullying: save evidence, block, report, tell an adult
Think before you post: would you be comfortable if a teacher saw this?
Verify news before sharing — misinformation spreads fast
practice_activities: Audit your social media privacy settings
Create a strong password for a mock account exercise

quiz.q: What is a digital footprint?
quiz.a: The trail of data you leave online through posts, searches, and messages

quiz.q: What should you do if you receive cyberbullying messages?
quiz.a: Save evidence, block the sender, and tell a trusted adult

personal_safety.important_note: Once something is posted online, it may never be fully deleted.

personal_safety.name: Personal Emergency Plan
learning_objectives: Create a personal emergency contact list
Agree a family meeting point
Know emergency service numbers
key_steps: Write down: 3 emergency contacts (name + number)
Agree a family meeting point if separated in an emergency
Know your local emergency numbers (police, fire, ambulance)
Put the list in your school bag
practice_activities: Create a physical emergency contact card with a parent
Memorise two key phone numbers

quiz.q: What is the emergency number in your country?
quiz.a: Varies by country — e.g. 999 (UK), 911 (USA), 112 (EU)

quiz.q: Where should you keep your emergency contact list?
quiz.a: In your school bag, in your phone, memorised

personal_safety.important_note: Update the contact list whenever family phone numbers change.

personal_safety.name: Playground Safety and Awareness
learning_objectives: Recognize safe versus unsafe playground behavior
Know what to do if separated from an adult
key_steps: Stay where a supervising adult can see you
Use equipment the way it was designed to be used
Tell an adult right away if a stranger talks to you
Stay near a friend or sibling
practice_activities: Role-play what to do if you get separated from your adult at the playground

quiz.q: What should you do if a stranger talks to you at the playground?
quiz.a: Move away and tell a trusted adult right away

personal_safety.important_note: Young children should always be supervised by a trusted adult at playgrounds.

personal_safety.name: Safe Walking to and from School
learning_objectives: Learn safe routes and crossing habits
Know who to ask for help along the way
key_steps: Always walk with a buddy or group when possible
Cross streets only at marked crossings with an adult or crossing guard
Know your route and stick to it
Never accept rides from someone you do not know
practice_activities: Walk the school route once with a parent and point out safe stopping places

quiz.q: Where should you cross the street?
quiz.a: At a marked crosswalk or with a crossing guard

personal_safety.important_note: Children should practice routes with a parent before walking independently.

personal_safety.name: Bicycle Safety Basics
learning_objectives: Understand helmet and gear safety
Learn basic road and path rules for young riders
key_steps: Always wear a properly fitted helmet
Ride on sidewalks or paths approved for children, not busy roads
Stop and look both ways before crossing
Ride with an adult until skills and judgment are ready
practice_activities: Practice a helmet fit check before every ride

quiz.q: What should you always wear when biking?
quiz.a: A properly fitted helmet

personal_safety.important_note: Adult supervision is recommended until a child can reliably follow traffic rules.

personal_safety.name: School Bus Safety Rules
learning_objectives: Learn safe boarding and riding behavior
Know the danger zone around a bus
key_steps: Wait for the bus a safe distance from the curb
Never walk behind a bus
Stay seated with a seatbelt if provided
Wait for the driver's signal before crossing in front of the bus
practice_activities: Practice identifying the bus danger zone using a picture or diagram

quiz.q: Where is it never safe to walk near a bus?
quiz.a: Behind the bus

personal_safety.important_note: Bus safety rules should be reinforced by parents and school staff regularly.

personal_safety.name: Family Safe Word and Check-In Code
learning_objectives: Understand why families use a secret safe word
Know when to use the safe word
key_steps: Agree on a private family safe word nobody else knows
Never go anywhere with someone who cannot say the safe word
Practice saying the safe word out loud together
Tell a trusted adult if someone asks for the word but seems unfamiliar
practice_activities: Create a family safe word together and practice a pretend pickup scenario

quiz.q: Why do families use a safe word?
quiz.a: To confirm that a person picking up a child is truly trusted

personal_safety.important_note: Choose a safe word together as a family and keep it private.

personal_safety.name: Meeting New Animals Safely
learning_objectives: Learn how to approach unfamiliar animals safely
Recognize warning signs from animals
key_steps: Always ask the owner before petting an animal
Let the animal sniff your hand first
Avoid running or screaming near strange animals
Tell an adult if a stray or aggressive animal approaches
practice_activities: Practice asking permission with a stuffed animal role-play

quiz.q: What should you do before petting a strange dog?
quiz.a: Ask the owner first

personal_safety.important_note: Adults should supervise young children around any unfamiliar animal.

personal_safety.name: Fire Drill and School Safety Routines
learning_objectives: Understand the purpose of school safety drills
Know how to follow drill instructions calmly
key_steps: Listen carefully to teacher instructions during drills
Walk quickly and quietly, do not run
Know your classroom's designated exit and meeting spot
Never go back inside for belongings
practice_activities: Practice walking calmly in a line to a pretend meeting spot

quiz.q: What should you never do during a fire drill?
quiz.a: Go back inside for belongings

personal_safety.important_note: School drills are supervised by teachers and staff for safety.

personal_safety.name: Safety at the Pool and Beach with Others
learning_objectives: Learn buddy-system rules around water
Know how to signal for help near water
key_steps: Always swim with a buddy and a supervising adult
Never go near water without permission
Learn to recognize a lifeguard and where they are
Call for help loudly if someone is struggling in water
practice_activities: Practice identifying the lifeguard stand and buddy check-ins during a pool visit

quiz.q: Who should always be present when a young child is near water?
quiz.a: A supervising adult

personal_safety.important_note: Adult supervision is required at all times near pools, beaches, and open water.

personal_safety.name: Recognizing Trusted Adults
learning_objectives: Learn to identify a short list of trusted adults
Understand the difference between trusted adults and strangers
key_steps: Make a list of trusted adults with a parent
Know that trusted adults do not ask you to keep secrets from parents
Feel comfortable telling any trusted adult if something feels wrong
Check with a parent before adding someone new to the list
practice_activities: Draw or list five trusted adults together with a parent

quiz.q: What is one sign an adult may not be trustworthy?
quiz.a: Asking you to keep a secret from your parents

personal_safety.important_note: Review and update the trusted adult list periodically with your child.

personal_safety.name: Saying No and Telling a Trusted Adult
learning_objectives: Build confidence to say no to uncomfortable requests
Understand that telling an adult is never tattling
key_steps: Practice saying "No" in a firm, clear voice
Walk or run away from the uncomfortable situation
Tell a trusted adult as soon as possible
Keep telling adults until someone listens and helps
practice_activities: Role-play saying no firmly to a pretend uncomfortable request

quiz.q: Is telling an adult about an uncomfortable situation considered tattling?
quiz.a: No, it is a safe and important thing to do

personal_safety.important_note: Reassure children that they will never be in trouble for telling the truth about feeling unsafe.

personal_safety.name: Stranger Danger at Malls and Public Places
learning_objectives: Recognize how to stay safe in crowded public places
Know what to do if lost in a mall or store
key_steps: Agree on a meeting spot with family before entering a crowded place
If separated, go to a checkout counter or uniformed staff member
Never leave with someone you do not know, even if they claim to know your parent
Stay in well-lit, busy areas
practice_activities: Practice identifying a store employee versus a stranger during a shopping trip

quiz.q: If you get lost in a mall, who should you ask for help?
quiz.a: A uniformed staff member or store employee

personal_safety.important_note: Practice this plan together before visiting busy public places.

personal_safety.name: Safety in Elevators and Escalators
learning_objectives: Learn safe elevator and escalator behavior
Recognize warning signs of an unsafe situation
key_steps: Stand near the control panel, not the back corner, when alone
Hold the handrail on escalators and avoid loose clothing near the edges
If someone makes you uncomfortable in an elevator, exit at the next floor
Avoid elevators with people who seem suspicious when possible
practice_activities: Practice locating the emergency button in a building elevator

quiz.q: What should you do if you feel unsafe in an elevator?
quiz.a: Exit at the next floor as soon as possible

personal_safety.important_note: Young children should use elevators and escalators with adult supervision.

personal_safety.name: Bullying Awareness and How to Respond
learning_objectives: Recognize different forms of bullying
Learn safe ways to respond and seek help
key_steps: Identify bullying behavior such as teasing, exclusion, or hitting
Use a firm voice and walk away when possible
Tell a trusted adult, such as a teacher or parent
Support a peer who is being bullied by including them or telling an adult
practice_activities: Role-play responding calmly to a teasing scenario

quiz.q: What should you do if you see someone being bullied?
quiz.a: Tell a trusted adult and, if safe, support the person being bullied

personal_safety.important_note: Encourage children to report bullying rather than handle it alone.

personal_safety.name: Cyberbullying Awareness and Response
learning_objectives: Recognize cyberbullying in messages, games, and social media
Learn how to respond and report it
key_steps: Do not respond to or forward mean messages
Save or screenshot the evidence
Block the person and report to the platform
Tell a parent or trusted adult right away
practice_activities: Practice using a platform's block and report features with a parent

quiz.q: What is the first step if you receive a mean message online?
quiz.a: Do not respond, save the evidence, and tell a trusted adult

personal_safety.important_note: Talk with a trusted adult before blocking or reporting so they can help document the issue.

personal_safety.name: Safe Passwords and Privacy Settings
learning_objectives: Learn how to create a strong password
Understand basic privacy settings on apps and devices
key_steps: Use long passwords mixing letters, numbers, and symbols
Never share passwords with friends, even close ones
Set social media and game profiles to private
Ask a parent before changing privacy settings
practice_activities: Practice creating a strong sample password together with a parent

quiz.q: Should you share your password with a close friend?
quiz.a: No, passwords should never be shared

personal_safety.important_note: Parents should help set up and review privacy settings for children's accounts.

personal_safety.name: Safe Gaming and Voice Chat Etiquette
learning_objectives: Learn safe habits for online gaming and voice chat
Recognize red flags from strangers in games
key_steps: Never share your real name, school, or address in games
Mute or block players who make you uncomfortable
Tell a parent if a stranger asks personal questions
Only add people you know in real life as friends
practice_activities: Review privacy and chat settings on a game together with a parent

quiz.q: What personal information should never be shared in online games?
quiz.a: Your real name, school, or address

personal_safety.important_note: Parents should monitor and periodically review children's online gaming interactions.

personal_safety.name: Recognizing Grooming Behavior Online
learning_objectives: Learn to recognize warning signs of grooming
Understand the importance of telling an adult immediately
key_steps: Be cautious of adults or strangers who give excessive compliments or gifts online
Notice requests to keep a friendship secret from parents
Never share photos or personal details with online-only contacts
Tell a trusted adult immediately about any uncomfortable online contact
practice_activities: Discuss real examples of grooming red flags with a parent or teacher

quiz.q: What is a common grooming red flag?
quiz.a: An adult asking to keep the relationship secret from parents

personal_safety.important_note: This topic should be discussed openly with a parent, teacher, or counselor.

personal_safety.name: Digital Footprint Awareness
learning_objectives: Understand that online posts can be permanent
Learn to think before posting
key_steps: Assume anything posted online could be seen by anyone, forever
Avoid posting your location in real time
Ask a parent before posting photos of yourself or friends
Search your own name occasionally with a parent to see what is public
practice_activities: Do a family search of a sample name to see what information appears publicly

quiz.q: Why should you think before posting something online?
quiz.a: Because it can be permanent and seen by many people

personal_safety.important_note: Review privacy settings with a parent regularly.

personal_safety.name: Safety at Sleepovers and Friends' Houses
learning_objectives: Learn what to check before staying overnight elsewhere
Know how to handle an uncomfortable situation
key_steps: Make sure a parent knows the address and contact number of the house
Keep a phone or way to contact a parent if needed
Trust your feelings if something seems wrong and call a parent
Know the family's fire exits and meeting point
practice_activities: Practice calling a parent from a friend's phone as a drill

quiz.q: What should a parent know before a sleepover?
quiz.a: The address and contact number of the host family

personal_safety.important_note: Parents should communicate with host families and confirm supervision plans.

personal_safety.name: Public Transport Safety Basics
learning_objectives: Learn safe habits for buses, trains, and taxis
Know how to handle getting lost or separated
key_steps: Stay close to a trusted adult and hold hands or bags in crowds
Know the stop name and route in advance
Sit near the driver or in view of staff when possible
If separated, stay where you are and ask staff for help
practice_activities: Practice reading a transit map with an adult before a trip

quiz.q: If you get separated on public transport, what should you do?
quiz.a: Stay put and ask a uniformed staff member for help

personal_safety.important_note: Children should use public transport with adult supervision until old enough to travel independently.

personal_safety.name: Safety at Large Public Events and Crowds
learning_objectives: Learn crowd safety basics
Know the family plan if separated in a crowd
key_steps: Agree on a meeting point before entering a crowded event
Wear bright or easily identifiable clothing
If separated, stay in one place and ask event staff or security for help
Avoid pushing through tight crowds
practice_activities: Pick a meeting point together before your next family outing

quiz.q: What should you do first if separated from family in a crowd?
quiz.a: Stay where you are and find event staff or security

personal_safety.important_note: Review the family meeting plan before every large event.

personal_safety.name: Basic Situational Awareness
learning_objectives: Learn to notice surroundings and possible risks
Build the habit of planning an exit or response
key_steps: Notice exits and safe adults when entering a new place
Keep phones and headphones down enough to hear surroundings
Trust uneasy feelings and move to a safer area
Walk confidently and stay aware, not distracted
practice_activities: Practice naming two exits the next time you enter a store or building

quiz.q: Why is it useful to notice exits when entering a building?
quiz.a: So you know how to leave quickly if something feels unsafe

personal_safety.important_note: Situational awareness is a lifelong skill best practiced regularly in everyday settings.

personal_safety.name: Trusting Your Instincts and Gut Feelings
learning_objectives: Understand that feelings of unease are worth listening to
Learn to act on instincts rather than ignore them
key_steps: Notice physical signs of unease, like a fast heartbeat
Leave a situation that feels wrong, even without a clear reason
Tell a trusted adult about the feeling right away
Remember it is okay to be wrong; safety comes first
practice_activities: Discuss a time you felt uneasy and what you did about it

quiz.q: Is it okay to leave a situation just because it feels wrong?
quiz.a: Yes, trusting instincts is an important safety skill

personal_safety.important_note: Reassure children that acting on instinct is never wrong, even if the situation turns out to be harmless.

personal_safety.name: Peer Pressure and Saying No
learning_objectives: Recognize peer pressure situations
Practice confident ways to say no
key_steps: Notice when friends push you to do something unsafe or uncomfortable
Use a simple, firm "No, I do not want to"
Suggest a different activity instead
Walk away and find a trusted adult if pressure continues
practice_activities: Role-play saying no to a peer pressure scenario

quiz.q: What is a simple way to respond to peer pressure?
quiz.a: A firm and clear "No, I do not want to"

personal_safety.important_note: Encourage open conversation with a trusted adult about peer pressure experiences.

personal_safety.name: Personal ID and Important Documents Awareness
learning_objectives: Learn why ID and documents matter
Know where family keeps important papers
key_steps: Know your full name, address, and a parent's phone number
Understand documents like birth certificates are kept safe at home
Never carry or show ID to strangers who ask
Ask a parent where family documents are stored in an emergency
practice_activities: Memorize a parent's phone number and practice reciting it

quiz.q: What personal information should every child memorize?
quiz.a: Full name, address, and a parent's phone number

personal_safety.important_note: Keep important documents in a safe, fire-resistant location known to trusted adults.

personal_safety.name: Safety When Home Alone
learning_objectives: Learn rules for staying home alone briefly
Know how to handle common situations like the doorbell or phone
key_steps: Never open the door to strangers
Do not tell callers or visitors that you are home alone
Know emergency numbers and a trusted neighbor's contact
Keep doors and windows locked while alone
practice_activities: Practice a pretend doorbell scenario with a parent

quiz.q: What should you say if a stranger asks if you are home alone?
quiz.a: Never confirm you are alone; say an adult is unavailable right now

personal_safety.important_note: Only leave children home alone briefly once age, maturity, and local guidelines support it, with clear rules set.

personal_safety.name: Reporting Abuse or Unsafe Situations
learning_objectives: Understand what abuse or neglect can look like
Learn there are safe adults and hotlines to report to
key_steps: Recognize signs that a situation is not okay, such as being hurt or scared
Tell a trusted adult, teacher, or counselor
Know that child helplines exist for reporting concerns
Keep telling adults until someone listens and helps
practice_activities: Identify three trusted adults at school who can help with a report

quiz.q: What should you do if telling one adult does not help?
quiz.a: Keep telling other trusted adults until someone helps

personal_safety.important_note: Reporting is always the right choice; children are never at fault for unsafe situations.

personal_safety.name: Recognizing and Avoiding Scams Aimed at Kids
learning_objectives: Learn common scam tactics targeting children
Understand why offers that sound too good are risky
key_steps: Be suspicious of prize, gift card, or free item offers online
Never click links or give information for a "free" prize
Ask a parent before entering any contest or giveaway
Report suspicious messages to a parent immediately
practice_activities: Look at a sample scam message together and identify the warning signs

quiz.q: What is a warning sign of an online scam?
quiz.a: An offer of a free prize that seems too good to be true

personal_safety.important_note: Review scam examples with a parent regularly as tactics change.

personal_safety.name: Basic First Aid for Personal Safety Incidents
learning_objectives: Learn simple first aid steps for minor injuries from unsafe situations
Know when to call for adult help
key_steps: Clean and cover minor cuts or scrapes
Apply a cold compress to bumps or bruises
Call an adult immediately for anything serious
Know how to dial local emergency services if no adult is available
practice_activities: Practice using a basic first aid kit under adult supervision

quiz.q: What should you do for a serious injury?
quiz.a: Call an adult or emergency services immediately

personal_safety.important_note: Basic first aid should be taught and supervised by a trained adult or first aid course.

personal_safety.name: Verbal Self-Defense and Assertiveness
learning_objectives: Build confident, assertive communication
Learn to set clear verbal boundaries
key_steps: Use a strong, clear voice and direct eye contact
State boundaries clearly, such as "Stop, I do not like that"
Stand tall and confident in body language
Walk away after stating a boundary if it is not respected
practice_activities: Practice assertive phrases in front of a mirror or with a trusted adult

quiz.q: What is an example of an assertive boundary statement?
quiz.a: "Stop, I do not like that" said in a clear, firm voice

personal_safety.important_note: Assertiveness training works best alongside real practice with trusted adults.

personal_safety.name: Babysitting Safety Basics
learning_objectives: Learn responsibilities and safety checks before babysitting
Know how to handle common emergencies while caring for children
key_steps: Get emergency contacts and house rules from parents in advance
Do a safety walkthrough of the home before parents leave
Know basic first aid and how to reach emergency services
Never leave young children unsupervised, even briefly
practice_activities: Complete a basic babysitting or first aid course before babysitting alone

quiz.q: What should a babysitter get from parents before they leave?
quiz.a: Emergency contacts and house safety rules

personal_safety.important_note: Many communities offer certified babysitting safety courses; taking one is recommended.

personal_safety.name: Safe Use of Ride-Sharing and Taxi Apps
learning_objectives: Learn how to verify a ride-share driver and vehicle
Know safety steps to take before, during, and after a ride
key_steps: Check the driver's name, photo, and license plate before entering
Share trip details live with a trusted contact
Sit in the back seat and keep the app's trip tracking on
Trust your instincts and exit if anything feels wrong
practice_activities: Practice checking a sample ride confirmation for matching details

quiz.q: What should you check before getting into a ride-share vehicle?
quiz.a: The driver's name, photo, and license plate match the app

personal_safety.important_note: Teens should use ride-sharing apps with parental knowledge and agreed safety rules.

personal_safety.name: Recognizing Phishing and Online Scams
learning_objectives: Learn to identify phishing emails and messages
Understand safe responses to suspicious requests
key_steps: Check sender addresses and links carefully before clicking
Never give passwords or personal information by email or text
Look for urgent or threatening language as a warning sign
Verify requests directly with the organization through official channels
practice_activities: Examine a sample phishing email and identify three warning signs

quiz.q: What is a common sign of a phishing message?
quiz.a: Urgent language pressuring you to click a link or share information quickly

personal_safety.important_note: When in doubt, verify a message independently rather than clicking any links.

personal_safety.name: Catfishing and Fake Profile Awareness
learning_objectives: Recognize signs of a fake online identity
Learn safe ways to verify who you are talking to
key_steps: Be cautious of profiles with few photos or a short history
Watch for inconsistent stories or refusal to video chat
Never send money or personal photos to an online-only contact
Tell a trusted adult about suspicious online relationships
practice_activities: Review a sample profile together and list signs it could be fake

quiz.q: What is a warning sign of a fake online profile?
quiz.a: Refusing to video chat or share consistent details

personal_safety.important_note: Discuss any online relationship concerns with a parent or trusted adult.

personal_safety.name: Safety in Unfamiliar Neighborhoods
learning_objectives: Learn how to navigate unfamiliar areas safely
Know how to plan ahead before visiting a new place
key_steps: Research the area and plan a route before going
Stay in well-lit, populated areas, especially after dark
Keep a charged phone and share your location with a trusted contact
Trust instincts and leave if the area feels unsafe
practice_activities: Plan a sample safe route to an unfamiliar location using a map app

quiz.q: What should you check before visiting an unfamiliar area?
quiz.a: The route, area reputation, and lighting conditions

personal_safety.important_note: Teens should share travel plans with a parent or guardian when exploring new areas.

personal_safety.name: Night-Time Outdoor Safety
learning_objectives: Learn safety habits for being outside after dark
Understand visibility and awareness at night
key_steps: Walk in well-lit, populated areas whenever possible
Wear bright or reflective clothing
Stay aware of surroundings rather than distracted by a phone
Travel with a friend or let someone know your route and return time
practice_activities: Plan a well-lit route for an evening walk with a friend or adult

quiz.q: Why is it safer to walk with a friend at night?
quiz.a: There is safety in numbers and someone can get help if needed

personal_safety.important_note: Younger teens should have adult awareness of any night-time outdoor plans.

personal_safety.name: Safety When Meeting Online Friends in Person
learning_objectives: Learn safe steps before meeting an online contact in real life
Understand the importance of parental involvement
key_steps: Always tell a parent or trusted adult about the plan first
Meet only in public, well-lit places with other people around
Bring a friend or have a trusted adult present nearby
Arrange your own transportation to and from the meeting
practice_activities: Practice explaining a meetup plan to a parent for feedback

quiz.q: Who should always know before meeting an online friend in person?
quiz.a: A parent or trusted adult

personal_safety.important_note: Meeting online contacts in person should always involve a parent's knowledge and, ideally, presence.

personal_safety.name: Consent and Personal Boundaries in Relationships
learning_objectives: Understand consent as an ongoing, clear agreement
Recognize the right to set and respect personal boundaries
key_steps: Understand that consent must be clear and can be withdrawn anytime
Respect a partner's or friend's stated boundaries
Communicate your own boundaries clearly and confidently
Talk to a trusted adult if a boundary is not respected
practice_activities: Discuss age-appropriate examples of respecting boundaries with a parent or educator

quiz.q: Can consent be withdrawn after it is given?
quiz.a: Yes, consent can be withdrawn at any time

personal_safety.important_note: This topic is best discussed with guidance from a parent, school counselor, or health educator.

personal_safety.name: Recognizing Coercive Control and Relationship Red Flags
learning_objectives: Learn warning signs of controlling or unhealthy relationships
Know where to get help if needed
key_steps: Notice excessive jealousy, isolation from friends, or constant monitoring
Recognize pressure or guilt used to control behavior
Talk to a trusted adult or counselor about concerning relationship patterns
Know that healthy relationships involve respect and trust
practice_activities: List qualities of a healthy relationship versus a controlling one

quiz.q: What is a red flag in an unhealthy relationship?
quiz.a: Attempts to isolate you from friends and family or control your actions

personal_safety.important_note: Discuss relationship concerns with a trusted adult, counselor, or helpline.

personal_safety.name: Basic Physical Self-Defense Awareness
learning_objectives: Learn the goal of self-defense is to escape, not fight
Understand basic principles of personal space and escape
key_steps: Create distance and look for an escape route first
Use a loud voice to draw attention and deter an attacker
Target vulnerable areas only if truly necessary to escape danger
Get to a safe, populated place and call for help immediately after
practice_activities: Take a basic self-defense class with a certified instructor

quiz.q: What is the primary goal of self-defense?
quiz.a: To escape safely, not to fight

personal_safety.important_note: Physical self-defense techniques should be learned from a certified instructor, with adult involvement for younger teens.

personal_safety.name: Personal Safety Devices: Whistles and Alarms
learning_objectives: Learn how personal alarms and whistles can help in an emergency
Know when and how to use them effectively
key_steps: Carry a whistle or personal alarm when walking alone
Use it loudly to attract attention if threatened
Keep the device easily accessible, not buried in a bag
Combine the device with moving toward people or safety
practice_activities: Practice using a whistle or alarm at a safe volume to learn how it sounds

quiz.q: Why carry a personal alarm or whistle?
quiz.a: To attract attention and deter a threat in an emergency

personal_safety.important_note: Personal safety devices are a helpful tool but should be combined with other safety habits.

personal_safety.name: Distracted Driving and Passenger Safety
learning_objectives: Understand the risks of distracted driving
Learn passenger responsibilities for safety
key_steps: Always wear a seatbelt, as driver or passenger
Avoid distracting a driver with noise or phone use
Speak up if a driver is distracted, tired, or driving unsafely
Know how to ask to be dropped off if a ride feels unsafe
practice_activities: Practice reminding a driver to buckle up before starting a trip

quiz.q: What is a passenger's responsibility if a driver seems unsafe?
quiz.a: Speak up and ask to stop or be dropped off safely

personal_safety.important_note: Learner drivers should always have a licensed adult supervising practice.

personal_safety.name: Campus and School Safety for Teens
learning_objectives: Learn school safety procedures and resources
Know how to report safety concerns at school
key_steps: Know the locations of school exits and safety officers
Follow lockdown and evacuation drill instructions carefully
Report suspicious behavior or threats to school staff immediately
Know who the school counselor or safety contact is
practice_activities: Locate the nearest two exits in each regular classroom

quiz.q: Who should you tell if you notice a safety threat at school?
quiz.a: A teacher, school staff member, or school safety officer

personal_safety.important_note: Follow your school's official safety and emergency procedures.

personal_safety.name: Safe Dating Practices for Teens
learning_objectives: Learn safety habits for dating and social outings
Understand the value of parental awareness of plans
key_steps: Tell a parent or trusted adult who you are meeting and where
Meet in public places for early dates
Arrange your own transportation to and from the date
Trust your instincts and have an exit plan if uncomfortable
practice_activities: Plan a sample safe first-date scenario and discuss it with a parent

quiz.q: Why is it safer to meet in a public place for an early date?
quiz.a: There are other people around who could help if needed

personal_safety.important_note: Parents should be aware of dating plans, especially for younger teens.

personal_safety.name: Identity Theft Prevention Basics
learning_objectives: Learn what personal information is sensitive
Understand basic steps to protect personal identity
key_steps: Never share Social Security or ID numbers online or by phone
Shred documents with personal information before discarding
Use strong, unique passwords for financial and school accounts
Check with a parent before sharing personal details on any form
practice_activities: Review a sample form together and identify which fields are sensitive

quiz.q: What should be done with documents containing personal information?
quiz.a: Shred them before discarding

personal_safety.important_note: Teens should involve a parent when managing any accounts containing personal information.

personal_safety.name: Stalking Awareness and Safety Planning
learning_objectives: Recognize signs of stalking behavior
Learn how to build a personal safety plan
key_steps: Document dates, times, and details of concerning contact
Vary routes and routines if being followed or watched
Inform trusted friends, family, and employers of the situation
Contact local police or a stalking hotline for support and a safety plan
practice_activities: Draft a basic personal safety plan including trusted contacts and documentation habits

quiz.q: Why is documenting incidents important in a stalking situation?
quiz.a: It provides evidence for law enforcement or legal action

personal_safety.important_note: Contact local law enforcement or a victim support hotline for stalking situations; this is informational only.

personal_safety.name: Workplace Safety Awareness
learning_objectives: Learn general workplace safety rights and practices
Know how to identify and report hazards
key_steps: Learn your workplace's emergency exits and procedures
Report unsafe equipment or conditions to a supervisor
Know your right to refuse clearly unsafe work in many jurisdictions
Keep emergency contact information updated with your employer
practice_activities: Locate your workplace's posted emergency evacuation plan

quiz.q: What should you do if you notice an unsafe workplace condition?
quiz.a: Report it to a supervisor or safety officer

personal_safety.important_note: Workplace safety rules vary by location and industry; follow your employer's official policies.

personal_safety.name: Workplace Harassment Awareness and Reporting
learning_objectives: Recognize different forms of workplace harassment
Learn safe, effective ways to report it
key_steps: Document incidents with dates, details, and witnesses if possible
Review your workplace's harassment reporting policy
Report to Human Resources or a designated safety officer
Seek support from trusted colleagues, friends, or professional organizations
practice_activities: Locate your workplace's harassment policy and reporting contact

quiz.q: What is a good first step after experiencing workplace harassment?
quiz.a: Document the incident and report it through official channels

personal_safety.important_note: Consult your employer's policy or local labor authority for formal guidance.

personal_safety.name: Safe Travel Alone: Hotel and Trip Safety
learning_objectives: Learn safety habits for solo travel
Know how to choose and secure accommodation
key_steps: Share your itinerary with a trusted contact at home
Choose reputable accommodations and verify entrances lock securely
Keep valuables secured and avoid displaying them publicly
Stay aware of surroundings and trust instincts in unfamiliar places
practice_activities: Create a simple travel safety checklist before your next trip

quiz.q: Why should you share your itinerary with someone at home?
quiz.a: So someone knows your plans if you cannot be reached

personal_safety.important_note: Research destination-specific safety guidance before traveling.

personal_safety.name: Elder Safety, Fraud, and Financial Scam Protection
learning_objectives: Recognize scams commonly targeting older adults
Learn protective steps for finances and personal information
key_steps: Never give personal or financial information to unsolicited callers
Verify requests independently through official phone numbers
Set up trusted contacts on financial accounts where available
Report suspected fraud to family, the bank, and local authorities promptly
practice_activities: Review a sample scam call script and identify red flags together

quiz.q: What should you do if an unsolicited caller asks for financial information?
quiz.a: Hang up and verify independently through an official number

personal_safety.important_note: Encourage older adults to discuss unusual financial requests with a trusted family member before acting.

emergency_preparedness.name: Fire Safety at Home
learning_objectives: Identify fire hazards
Know the stop-drop-roll technique
Plan and practise a home fire escape
key_steps: Identify common fire hazards: candles, unattended stoves, overloaded sockets
Stop, Drop, Roll if clothing catches fire
Plan two exit routes from every room
Agree a meeting point outside
Call emergency services from outside — never go back in
practice_activities: Walk through your home escape routes with a family member
Practise stop-drop-roll in an open area

quiz.q: What should you do if your clothes catch fire?
quiz.a: Stop, drop to the ground, and roll to smother the flames

quiz.q: Where should you meet your family after escaping a fire?
quiz.a: At a pre-agreed safe meeting point outside

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Never go back into a burning building for any reason.

emergency_preparedness.name: Earthquake Safety
learning_objectives: Identify safe spots during an earthquake
Know the drop-cover-hold technique
Know what to do after shaking stops
key_steps: Drop to hands and knees
Cover your head and neck under a sturdy table or against an interior wall
Hold on until shaking stops
After: check for injuries, expect aftershocks
Stay away from damaged buildings and power lines
practice_activities: Practise drop-cover-hold at school or home
Identify safe spots in your classroom

quiz.q: What is the correct response during an earthquake?
quiz.a: Drop, Cover, Hold — get under a sturdy surface and protect your head

quiz.q: What should you do after an earthquake stops?
quiz.a: Check for injuries, expect aftershocks, and move to open ground away from buildings

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Knowing in advance what to do removes panic in a real event.

emergency_preparedness.name: Flood Safety
learning_objectives: Understand flood warning signs
Know what to do if caught in flooding
Prepare a flood emergency kit
key_steps: Move to higher ground immediately
Never walk or drive through floodwater — 15 cm can knock you down
Turn off electricity at the mains if safe to do so
Emergency kit: torch, water, food, first aid, phone charger
Listen to emergency service announcements
practice_activities: Prepare a simple emergency kit list with a parent
Discuss your home's flood risk and escape routes

quiz.q: How shallow can floodwater be and still knock a person down?
quiz.a: 15 cm (6 inches)

quiz.q: Name two items for a flood emergency kit.
quiz.a: Torch, bottled water, food, first aid kit, phone charger (any two)

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Never attempt to cross floodwater on foot or in a vehicle — it is extremely dangerous.

emergency_preparedness.name: Storm and Cyclone Safety
learning_objectives: Identify warning signs of a severe storm
Know how to take shelter safely
Avoid common storm dangers
key_steps: Monitor weather warnings and alerts
Move indoors — away from windows
Avoid trees, water, and metal objects
If outdoors and lightning strikes: crouch low, spread out from others
Do not use landline phones during lightning
After storm: check for hazards before going outside
practice_activities: Identify the safest room in your home during a storm
Create a storm safety checklist with a parent

quiz.q: Where should you shelter during a severe storm?
quiz.a: Inside a sturdy building, away from windows

quiz.q: Why avoid trees during lightning?
quiz.a: Trees are tall and attract lightning strikes

emergency_preparedness.important_note: A charged portable phone and emergency kit should be ready before storm season.

emergency_preparedness.name: Safe Drinking Water
learning_objectives: Identify safe and unsafe water sources
Know basic water purification methods
Understand hygiene when water is limited
key_steps: Running, treated tap water is safest
Boiling: bring to a rolling boil for 1 full minute (adult required)
Collect rainwater if tap water is unavailable
Never drink from stagnant water sources
Store purified water in a clean sealed container
practice_activities: Demonstrate boiling water with adult supervision
Discuss what makes water contaminated

quiz.q: How long should you boil water to make it safe to drink?
quiz.a: 1 full minute at a rolling boil

quiz.q: Name one sign that water may be unsafe.
quiz.a: Cloudy, smells bad, stagnant, or comes from an unknown source

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Boiling requires adult supervision — never leave a fire or stove unattended.

emergency_preparedness.name: Emergency Signalling
learning_objectives: Learn three universal distress signals
Use a whistle and mirror signal correctly
Understand when and how to signal for help
key_steps: Universal distress: three of any signal (whistle, fire, mirror flash)
Whistle: three short blasts, pause, repeat
Mirror signal: reflect sunlight at aircraft or rescue teams
Ground signals: stamp SOS in sand or snow
Stay in one place so rescuers can find you
practice_activities: Practise the three-blast whistle signal
Demonstrate a mirror-flash with a reflective surface in sunlight

quiz.q: What is the universal distress signal number?
quiz.a: Three — three blasts, three fires, three flashes

quiz.q: What letters should you stamp in the ground to signal SOS?
quiz.a: SOS

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Stay calm and conserve energy while waiting for rescue.

emergency_preparedness.name: Emergency Kit Preparation
learning_objectives: Identify essential items for a 72-hour emergency kit
Pack and maintain a kit at home
Know how long to store food and water
key_steps: Water: 3 litres per person per day for 3 days
Non-perishable food for 3 days
First aid kit and prescribed medications
Torch and extra batteries
Phone charger and emergency radio
Important documents in a waterproof bag
Change of clothes and warm blanket
Review kit every 6 months
practice_activities: Pack a 72-hour emergency kit with a parent
Check expiry dates and rotate food supplies

quiz.q: How much water should you store per person per day?
quiz.a: At least 3 litres

quiz.q: How often should you check your emergency kit?
quiz.a: Every 6 months

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Store your kit in an easy-to-carry bag near the main exit.

emergency_preparedness.name: Heat and Cold Safety
learning_objectives: Recognise signs of heat exhaustion and hypothermia
Know how to prevent heat and cold illness
Respond appropriately to temperature emergencies
key_steps: Heat exhaustion: heavy sweating, weakness, cool pale skin — move to shade, give water, loosen clothing
Heat stroke: very high temperature, red dry skin, confusion — call emergency immediately
Hypothermia: shivering, confusion, slurred speech — warm slowly, add layers, call for help
Frostbite: numb, pale, hard skin — rewarm gently, do not rub
practice_activities: Create a heat safety checklist for summer outings
Practise identifying signs using case-study scenarios

quiz.q: Name two signs of heat exhaustion.
quiz.a: Heavy sweating, weakness, nausea, pale cool skin

quiz.q: What is the first action for suspected heat stroke?
quiz.a: Call emergency services immediately — it is life-threatening

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Stay hydrated and seek shade in hot weather; layer up and stay dry in cold.

emergency_preparedness.name: Fire Drill Practice at Home
learning_objectives: Learn what to do when a smoke alarm sounds
Practice a calm, quick exit from the home
key_steps: Get low and go to the nearest safe exit when the alarm sounds
Never hide from a fire; go to the family meeting spot outside
Practice two ways out of every room
Call for help once outside; never go back inside
practice_activities: Practice a home fire drill with a parent twice a year

quiz.q: What should you do if you hear a smoke alarm?
quiz.a: Get low, go to the nearest exit, and meet outside at the family spot

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Practice home fire drills regularly with a parent or guardian.

emergency_preparedness.name: Knowing Your Home Address and Emergency Numbers
learning_objectives: Memorize home address and key emergency numbers
Understand when to use this information
key_steps: Learn your full home address by heart
Memorize a parent's phone number
Know the local emergency number for your country
Practice reciting this information clearly and calmly
practice_activities: Sing or repeat the address and numbers until memorized

quiz.q: What is the local emergency number you should know?
quiz.a: It varies by country; know your local one, such as 911, 112, or 999

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Emergency numbers vary by country; confirm the correct one for your area.

emergency_preparedness.name: What to Do If You Smell Smoke
learning_objectives: Recognize smoke as a fire warning sign
Learn the correct immediate response
key_steps: Alert an adult immediately if you smell or see smoke
Do not investigate the source yourself
Get low and head to the nearest exit if told to leave
Meet at the family's outside meeting spot
practice_activities: Practice describing what to do if smoke is smelled during a pretend scenario

quiz.q: Should a child investigate the source of smoke alone?
quiz.a: No, always alert an adult immediately

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Children should never attempt to locate or fight a fire themselves.

emergency_preparedness.name: Stop, Drop, and Roll Basics
learning_objectives: Learn what to do if clothing catches fire
Practice the stop, drop, and roll technique
key_steps: Stop moving immediately, do not run
Drop to the ground right away
Cover your face with your hands
Roll back and forth until the flames are out
practice_activities: Practice the stop, drop, and roll motion on a soft, safe surface

quiz.q: What should you do first if your clothing catches fire?
quiz.a: Stop moving immediately, do not run

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Practice this technique with adult supervision on a soft surface.

emergency_preparedness.name: Meeting Point Planning for Families
learning_objectives: Understand why families choose an outside meeting spot
Know your family's meeting spot
key_steps: Choose a safe spot outside and a safe distance from the home
Practice walking to the spot during a drill
Know that everyone should go straight there in an emergency
Never go back inside once at the meeting spot
practice_activities: Walk to your family's meeting spot together and time it

quiz.q: Where should everyone go during a home emergency?
quiz.a: The family's agreed outside meeting spot

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Choose a meeting spot together with the whole family and revisit it yearly.

emergency_preparedness.name: Thunderstorm and Lightning Safety
learning_objectives: Learn safe behavior during thunderstorms
Understand the danger of lightning outdoors
key_steps: Go inside a sturdy building or hard-topped vehicle when thunder is heard
Stay away from windows during a storm
Avoid water, tall trees, and metal objects outdoors
Wait 30 minutes after the last thunder before going back outside
practice_activities: Practice the "when thunder roars, go indoors" rule during the next storm

quiz.q: How long should you wait after the last thunder before going outside?
quiz.a: About 30 minutes

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Adults should supervise children indoors during thunderstorms.

emergency_preparedness.name: Safety During a Power Outage
learning_objectives: Learn what to do when the lights go out unexpectedly
Recognize safe light and heat sources
key_steps: Stay calm and use a flashlight, not candles, for light
Keep the refrigerator closed to keep food cold
Stay away from downed power lines if outside
Wait with an adult for power to be restored
practice_activities: Locate the family flashlight together and check the batteries

quiz.q: What should you use for light during a power outage instead of candles?
quiz.a: A flashlight

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Keep flashlights and batteries in an easy-to-find location for outages.

emergency_preparedness.name: Basic Emergency Call Practice
learning_objectives: Learn when and how to call for emergency help
Practice speaking clearly to a dispatcher
key_steps: Only call emergency numbers for real emergencies
State your name, address, and what is happening clearly
Stay on the line and answer the dispatcher's questions
Do not hang up until told it is okay
practice_activities: Practice a pretend emergency call with a parent using a toy phone

quiz.q: What information should you give first in an emergency call?
quiz.a: Your name, address, and what is happening

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Practice this only with a trusted adult using a disconnected or toy phone.

emergency_preparedness.name: Tornado Safety Basics
learning_objectives: Recognize tornado warning signs and alerts
Learn the safest place to shelter during a tornado
key_steps: Go to a basement or small interior room on the lowest floor
Stay away from windows and cover your head and neck
Listen to a weather radio or phone alert for updates
Know the difference between a tornado watch and a tornado warning
practice_activities: Practice a tornado drill by moving quickly to the safest room at home

quiz.q: What is the safest place to shelter during a tornado?
quiz.a: A small interior room or basement on the lowest floor, away from windows

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Follow official weather alerts and local emergency guidance during tornado season.

emergency_preparedness.name: Wildfire Awareness and Evacuation Basics
learning_objectives: Recognize wildfire risk signs
Learn the basics of a wildfire evacuation plan
key_steps: Know your community's evacuation routes and alerts
Keep a go-bag ready during high wildfire risk seasons
Follow official evacuation orders immediately, do not wait
Close windows and doors when leaving to slow fire spread
practice_activities: Review your family's wildfire evacuation route on a map

quiz.q: What should you do when an evacuation order is given?
quiz.a: Leave immediately following the official route

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Always follow official evacuation orders from local fire and emergency authorities.

emergency_preparedness.name: Family Communication Plan During Disasters
learning_objectives: Learn why families need a communication plan
Know how to reconnect if separated
key_steps: Choose an out-of-area contact everyone can call
Memorize or write down key phone numbers
Agree on backup meeting locations if home is not accessible
Practice texting, since texts may work when calls do not
practice_activities: Create a family contact card with numbers and meeting points

quiz.q: Why choose an out-of-area contact for a family plan?
quiz.a: Local lines may be busy, but a distant contact is often easier to reach

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Update the family communication plan yearly or after any address change.

emergency_preparedness.name: Evacuation Route Planning
learning_objectives: Learn how to plan a safe evacuation route
Understand backup route planning
key_steps: Identify at least two ways out of your neighborhood
Keep a paper map as backup in case phones lose signal
Practice driving or walking the routes with a family member
Know where local shelters are along each route
practice_activities: Draw a simple map of two evacuation routes from your home

quiz.q: Why is it useful to know more than one evacuation route?
quiz.a: The main route may be blocked or unsafe during an emergency

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Practice evacuation routes with an adult before an emergency occurs.

emergency_preparedness.name: Sheltering in Place vs Evacuating
learning_objectives: Understand the difference between sheltering in place and evacuating
Learn how to decide which applies to a given emergency
key_steps: Follow official guidance on whether to shelter or evacuate
Shelter in place by sealing windows and doors if instructed for airborne hazards
Evacuate immediately if told to, taking your emergency kit
Keep a radio or phone on for updated instructions
practice_activities: Discuss with family which emergencies call for sheltering versus evacuating

quiz.q: Who decides whether to shelter in place or evacuate?
quiz.a: Local emergency officials, through official alerts

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Always follow official instructions from local emergency management authorities.

emergency_preparedness.name: Disaster Supply Kit for Pets
learning_objectives: Learn what pets need during an emergency
Understand how to include pets in a family plan
key_steps: Pack food, water, and medication for pets in the kit
Include a leash, carrier, and copies of vaccination records
Know which shelters or hotels accept pets in your area
Update pet identification tags with current contact information
practice_activities: Assemble a small pet emergency kit with a parent

quiz.q: What documents should be kept for pets in an emergency kit?
quiz.a: Vaccination records and identification information

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Research pet-friendly shelters in your area ahead of time.

emergency_preparedness.name: Basic Emergency Radio Use
learning_objectives: Learn how a battery or hand-crank radio works
Understand why radios matter when power or cell service is down
key_steps: Keep a battery or hand-crank emergency radio in your kit
Know how to tune to local emergency broadcast stations
Change or charge batteries regularly
Use the radio only for updates, not to drain batteries unnecessarily
practice_activities: Practice tuning a hand-crank radio to a local station

quiz.q: Why is an emergency radio useful during a power outage?
quiz.a: It can receive updates when cell service or power is unavailable

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Keep spare batteries or a hand-crank model in your emergency kit.

emergency_preparedness.name: Water Purification Methods
learning_objectives: Learn basic ways to make water safer to drink in an emergency
Understand when purified water is necessary
key_steps: Boil water for at least one minute to kill most germs
Use water purification tablets if boiling is not possible
Use a proper water filter rated for removing pathogens
Never drink untreated water from unknown sources
practice_activities: Practice reading the instructions on water purification tablets with an adult

quiz.q: How long should water be boiled to make it safer to drink?
quiz.a: At least one minute (longer at high altitude)

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Water purification should be supervised by an adult, especially boiling water.

emergency_preparedness.name: Food Storage for Emergencies
learning_objectives: Learn what foods store well for emergencies
Understand basic food safety during outages
key_steps: Store non-perishable foods like canned goods, rice, and dried fruit
Rotate emergency food supplies before they expire
Keep a manual can opener with the emergency kit
Throw away perishable food after a long power outage to avoid illness
practice_activities: Check expiration dates on the family's emergency food supply

quiz.q: Why should emergency food supplies be rotated?
quiz.a: To make sure the food does not expire before it is needed

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Check and rotate emergency food supplies at least once a year.

emergency_preparedness.name: Tsunami Safety Basics
learning_objectives: Recognize natural warning signs of a tsunami
Learn the correct response to a tsunami warning
key_steps: Move immediately to high ground after an earthquake near the coast
Do not wait for an official alert if natural signs like receding water appear
Stay away from the coast until officials say it is safe
Know your community's tsunami evacuation routes
practice_activities: Locate the nearest high ground point from your coastal home or hotel

quiz.q: What natural sign can indicate an incoming tsunami?
quiz.a: Water suddenly receding far from the shore

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Follow official tsunami warnings and evacuation instructions immediately.

emergency_preparedness.name: Volcanic Eruption Awareness
learning_objectives: Learn basic volcanic hazards like ash and lava flows
Understand safety steps during an eruption warning
key_steps: Follow official evacuation orders near an active volcano
Wear a mask or cover your mouth and nose to avoid ash inhalation
Stay indoors with windows closed if ashfall is occurring
Keep goggles or glasses on hand to protect eyes from ash
practice_activities: Research whether your region has any volcanic risk and local plans

quiz.q: What should you cover during heavy volcanic ashfall?
quiz.a: Your mouth and nose with a mask or cloth

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Follow guidance from local geological and emergency authorities near active volcanoes.

emergency_preparedness.name: Post-Disaster Safety: Checking for Hazards
learning_objectives: Learn what hazards can remain after a disaster
Understand how to stay safe when returning home
key_steps: Check for gas leaks, damaged wires, and structural damage before entering
Avoid floodwater, which can be contaminated or electrically charged
Wear sturdy shoes to avoid debris injuries
Take photos of damage for insurance before cleaning up
practice_activities: Walk through a checklist of hazards to look for after a storm

quiz.q: Why should you avoid floodwater after a disaster?
quiz.a: It can be contaminated or hide electrical or structural hazards

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Let trained adults or professionals inspect for gas, electrical, or structural hazards.

emergency_preparedness.name: What to Expect When First Responders Arrive
learning_objectives: Learn how to interact safely with first responders
Understand what information to share
key_steps: Stay calm and follow instructions from firefighters, police, or paramedics
Answer questions clearly and honestly
Point out anyone who is injured or trapped
Move out of the way to let responders work safely
practice_activities: Practice describing an emergency situation clearly and calmly

quiz.q: What should you do when first responders arrive?
quiz.a: Stay calm, follow their instructions, and answer questions clearly

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Cooperating clearly with first responders helps them help you faster.

emergency_preparedness.name: Community Emergency Resources: Shelters and Hotlines
learning_objectives: Learn what community resources exist during emergencies
Know how to find shelters and helplines
key_steps: Know the location of the nearest emergency shelter
Save local emergency hotline numbers in a phone or on paper
Understand that shelters provide food, water, and safety information
Ask local officials or a radio broadcast for shelter locations if unsure
practice_activities: Look up your community's nearest designated emergency shelter

quiz.q: What kind of help can an emergency shelter provide?
quiz.a: Food, water, safety information, and a safe place to stay

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Confirm current shelter locations with local emergency management, as they can change.

emergency_preparedness.name: School Lockdown and Emergency Drills
learning_objectives: Understand the purpose of school lockdown drills
Learn how to follow instructions during a drill
key_steps: Follow teacher instructions quickly and quietly
Move away from doors and windows as directed
Stay silent and still until told the drill or event is over
Know your classroom's specific safety procedure
practice_activities: Review your school's lockdown procedure with a teacher or parent

quiz.q: What should you do during a school lockdown drill?
quiz.a: Follow the teacher's instructions quickly and stay quiet and still

emergency_preparedness.important_note: School drills are supervised by trained staff for student safety.

emergency_preparedness.name: Severe Weather Alerts and Warnings
learning_objectives: Learn the difference between a watch and a warning
Know how to receive severe weather alerts
key_steps: A watch means conditions are possible; a warning means it is happening or imminent
Turn on a weather radio, app, or local news for updates
Follow instructions given with each type of alert
Keep a phone charged to receive emergency alerts
practice_activities: Set up severe weather alerts on a family phone or device

quiz.q: What is the difference between a weather watch and a warning?
quiz.a: A watch means conditions are possible; a warning means it is happening or imminent

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Enable official emergency alert notifications on household devices.

emergency_preparedness.name: Safe Use of Flashlights and Emergency Lighting
learning_objectives: Learn safe habits with flashlights and emergency lights
Understand battery and light safety
key_steps: Keep a flashlight within reach in every bedroom
Never use candles as a substitute due to fire risk
Check and replace batteries regularly
Use glow sticks as a safer alternative for young children if needed
practice_activities: Test all household flashlights and replace weak batteries

quiz.q: Why are candles not recommended during a power outage?
quiz.a: They pose a fire risk, especially unsupervised

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Adults should supervise young children when using any emergency lighting.

emergency_preparedness.name: Building a Family Emergency Plan Document
learning_objectives: Learn how to compile a full written family emergency plan
Understand what information the plan should include
key_steps: List emergency contacts, meeting points, and evacuation routes
Include medical information and any special needs of family members
Store copies at home, at work or school, and with an out-of-area contact
Review and update the plan at least once a year
practice_activities: Draft a one-page family emergency plan with a parent

quiz.q: How often should a family emergency plan be reviewed?
quiz.a: At least once a year, or after any major life change

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Share copies of the completed plan with all family members and caregivers.

emergency_preparedness.name: Chemical Spill and Hazmat Awareness
learning_objectives: Recognize hazardous material warning signs
Learn safe response steps to a chemical spill
key_steps: Move upwind and away from the spill area immediately
Do not touch or attempt to clean up unknown substances
Report the spill to emergency services with location details
Follow official instructions on shelter-in-place or evacuation
practice_activities: Learn to recognize common hazmat placard symbols

quiz.q: What should you do if you encounter an unknown chemical spill?
quiz.a: Move away immediately and report it to emergency services

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Never attempt to handle or clean up hazardous materials yourself; leave it to trained responders.

emergency_preparedness.name: Pandemic and Illness Outbreak Preparedness
learning_objectives: Learn basic steps to prepare for a disease outbreak
Understand hygiene practices that reduce spread
key_steps: Keep a basic supply of masks, soap, and hand sanitizer
Follow official public health guidance on precautions
Stock a few weeks of essential supplies during outbreak warnings
Stay informed through official health authority updates, not rumors
practice_activities: Check your household's supply of basic hygiene and health items

quiz.q: Where should you get outbreak guidance from?
quiz.a: Official public health authorities, not rumors or social media

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Follow guidance from recognized public health organizations such as the WHO or your national health agency.

emergency_preparedness.name: Financial Emergency Preparedness: Documents and Cash
learning_objectives: Learn what documents and funds to prepare for emergencies
Understand why cash and copies matter when systems are down
key_steps: Keep copies of ID, insurance, and medical documents in a waterproof folder
Store a small amount of emergency cash, since card systems may fail
Keep digital backups of key documents in secure cloud storage
Update the emergency document folder yearly
practice_activities: Assemble a family emergency document folder with a parent

quiz.q: Why is emergency cash useful during a disaster?
quiz.a: Card payment systems and ATMs may not work during power or network outages

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Keep emergency documents and cash somewhere quickly accessible during an evacuation.

emergency_preparedness.name: Generator Safety Basics
learning_objectives: Learn the dangers of improper generator use
Understand safe generator placement and operation
key_steps: Never run a generator indoors, in a garage, or near windows
Keep the generator at least 20 feet from the home, exhaust pointed away
Let the generator cool before refueling
Install carbon monoxide detectors near sleeping areas as a backup precaution
practice_activities: Review the household generator's manual and safe placement spot with an adult

quiz.q: Why should a generator never run indoors?
quiz.a: It produces carbon monoxide, which can be deadly in enclosed spaces

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Generators must be operated outdoors by an adult following the manufacturer's instructions.

emergency_preparedness.name: Carbon Monoxide Awareness and Detection
learning_objectives: Learn the dangers of carbon monoxide
Understand how to detect and respond to it
key_steps: Install carbon monoxide detectors near sleeping areas
Recognize symptoms like headache, dizziness, and nausea
Get to fresh air immediately if a detector sounds
Never use grills, generators, or camp stoves indoors
practice_activities: Test the household carbon monoxide detector with an adult

quiz.q: What should you do if a carbon monoxide detector sounds?
quiz.a: Get to fresh air immediately and call emergency services

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Carbon monoxide is odorless and colorless; detectors are essential and should be tested regularly.

emergency_preparedness.name: Landslide and Mudslide Awareness
learning_objectives: Recognize warning signs of a landslide or mudslide
Learn safe evacuation behavior in risk areas
key_steps: Watch for cracking ground, tilting trees, or unusual sounds
Move away and uphill from the path of a slide immediately
Avoid river valleys and canyons during heavy rain in risk areas
Follow official evacuation orders in landslide-prone regions
practice_activities: Research whether your area has any landslide risk zones

quiz.q: What is a warning sign of an incoming landslide?
quiz.a: Cracking ground, tilting trees, or unusual rumbling sounds

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Follow local geological survey and emergency management guidance in landslide-prone areas.

emergency_preparedness.name: Extreme Drought and Water Shortage Preparedness
learning_objectives: Learn how to prepare for extended water shortages
Understand basic water conservation steps
key_steps: Store a supply of clean water for drinking and basic hygiene
Follow local water restriction guidelines during drought
Reduce non-essential water use, like lawn watering, during shortages
Know where community water distribution points are, if activated
practice_activities: Calculate how much stored water your household would need for two weeks

quiz.q: How much water is generally recommended per person per day for storage?
quiz.a: About one gallon (roughly four liters) per person per day

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Follow local authority guidance on water restrictions and storage limits.

emergency_preparedness.name: Preparing an Emergency Car Kit
learning_objectives: Learn what items belong in a vehicle emergency kit
Understand when and how to use them
key_steps: Include water, blankets, a flashlight, and a first aid kit
Add jumper cables, a tire gauge, and basic tools
Keep a phone charger and paper map in the car
Check and refresh the kit every season
practice_activities: Assemble or check a car emergency kit with a parent

quiz.q: Why should a car emergency kit be checked seasonally?
quiz.a: Needs change with weather, such as adding blankets in winter

emergency_preparedness.important_note: An adult should assemble and maintain the vehicle emergency kit.

emergency_preparedness.name: Safety During Extended Evacuation Shelter Stays
learning_objectives: Learn what to expect at an emergency shelter
Understand basic etiquette and safety in shared shelter spaces
key_steps: Bring identification and essential medications to the shelter
Follow shelter staff instructions and posted rules
Keep track of family members and a shared meeting point inside the shelter
Report any unsafe conditions to shelter staff
practice_activities: List the key items to bring if staying at an emergency shelter

quiz.q: What should you bring to an emergency shelter?
quiz.a: Identification, essential medications, and basic personal supplies

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Follow the specific guidance of shelter staff and local emergency management.

emergency_preparedness.name: Basic Wilderness Emergency Signaling for Hikers
learning_objectives: Learn simple signals to attract rescuer attention outdoors
Understand the universal distress signal pattern
key_steps: Use three of anything, three whistle blasts, three fires, or three flashes, as a distress signal
Use a mirror or bright object to signal aircraft on sunny days
Stay in an open area to be visible to search teams
Stay put once lost rather than wandering further
practice_activities: Practice the three-signal distress pattern with a whistle under adult supervision

quiz.q: What is the universal distress signal pattern in the wilderness?
quiz.a: A group of three, such as three whistle blasts or three fires

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Wilderness signaling should be practiced with an experienced adult or guide.

emergency_preparedness.name: Home Utility Shutoff Basics: Gas, Water, Electric
learning_objectives: Learn the location of home utility shutoffs
Understand when it is safe to shut off utilities
key_steps: Know the location of the main gas, water, and electric shutoffs
Shut off gas only if you smell gas or are instructed to after an earthquake
Turn off the main water valve if a major pipe bursts
Never turn gas back on yourself; call the utility company
practice_activities: Locate all three main utility shutoffs at home with an adult

quiz.q: Who should turn the gas supply back on after it has been shut off?
quiz.a: The gas utility company or a trained professional, never yourself

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Utility shutoff valves should be identified and used only under adult guidance.

emergency_preparedness.name: Preparing for Extended School or Workplace Lockdowns
learning_objectives: Learn how to prepare for a longer lockdown situation
Understand personal readiness steps
key_steps: Keep a small personal kit with water, snacks, and any needed medication
Know your school or workplace's specific lockdown procedures
Stay quiet, follow staff instructions, and avoid using phones loudly
Know how communication with family will happen during a lockdown
practice_activities: Review your school or workplace's lockdown policy

quiz.q: What should a personal lockdown kit include?
quiz.a: Water, a snack, and any necessary medication

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Follow your institution's official lockdown procedures and staff instructions.

emergency_preparedness.name: Understanding Emergency Alert Systems
learning_objectives: Learn how national and local emergency alert systems work
Understand how to receive and respond to alerts
key_steps: Enable wireless emergency alerts on mobile devices
Understand the different alert levels used in your country
Follow the specific instructions given in each alert
Do not ignore repeated or test alerts, as some indicate real events
practice_activities: Check that emergency alerts are enabled on household phones

quiz.q: What should you do when you receive an emergency alert?
quiz.a: Read it carefully and follow its specific instructions

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Alert systems vary by country; learn the specific system used in your region.

emergency_preparedness.name: Preparing a Go-Bag for Rapid Evacuation
learning_objectives: Learn what a go-bag is and why it matters
Understand what to pack for quick evacuation
key_steps: Pack essential documents, medications, and a change of clothes
Include water, snacks, a flashlight, and a phone charger
Keep the bag in an easily accessible location
Check and refresh contents every six months
practice_activities: Assemble a personal go-bag and review its contents with a parent

quiz.q: How often should a go-bag be checked and refreshed?
quiz.a: Roughly every six months

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Keep the go-bag light enough to carry quickly and store it near an exit.

emergency_preparedness.name: Nuclear or Radiological Incident Awareness
learning_objectives: Learn basic protective actions for a radiological incident
Understand the concept of shelter, distance, and time
key_steps: Get inside a sturdy building immediately if instructed
Stay away from windows and seal gaps if advised
Remove and bag outer clothing if contamination is suspected
Follow official instructions closely; do not rely on assumptions
practice_activities: Review official government guidance on radiological emergency response

quiz.q: What are the three basic protective concepts in a radiological incident?
quiz.a: Shelter, distance from the source, and limiting exposure time

emergency_preparedness.important_note: This is informational only; follow official government and emergency management guidance in an actual incident.

emergency_preparedness.name: Severe Air Quality and Smoke Preparedness
learning_objectives: Learn how to protect health during poor air quality events
Understand when to limit outdoor activity
key_steps: Check local air quality index readings regularly during smoke events
Keep windows closed and use air filtration if available
Wear a properly rated mask outdoors when air quality is very poor
