Limit strenuous outdoor activity during unhealthy air quality days
practice_activities: Check your local air quality index reading and its meaning

quiz.q: What should you check before heavy outdoor activity during wildfire season?
quiz.a: The local air quality index

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Follow local health authority guidance during poor air quality events, especially for at-risk individuals.

emergency_preparedness.name: Coordinating Neighborhood Emergency Response
learning_objectives: Learn the value of neighborhood-level emergency coordination
Understand basic community preparedness roles
key_steps: Get to know neighbors and any special needs they may have
Identify neighbors with useful skills, such as first aid training
Establish a simple neighborhood communication method for emergencies
Participate in or organize a community emergency preparedness meeting
practice_activities: Organize or attend a neighborhood emergency preparedness meeting

quiz.q: Why is neighborhood coordination valuable in emergencies?
quiz.a: Neighbors can often provide the fastest help before official responders arrive

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Coordinate with local emergency management offices for community preparedness resources.

emergency_preparedness.name: Insurance and Property Documentation for Disasters
learning_objectives: Learn how to document property for insurance purposes
Understand what records help after a disaster
key_steps: Photograph or video household belongings and property regularly
Keep insurance policy numbers and contacts easily accessible
Store documentation copies in cloud storage and offsite
Update documentation after major purchases or renovations
practice_activities: Do a walkthrough video of your home for insurance records

quiz.q: Why should property be documented before a disaster occurs?
quiz.a: It helps support insurance claims for lost or damaged belongings

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Consult your insurance provider for specific documentation requirements.

emergency_preparedness.name: Emergency Preparedness for Elderly or Disabled Family Members
learning_objectives: Learn how to adapt emergency plans for special needs
Understand additional supplies and considerations needed
key_steps: Include necessary medical equipment, medications, and mobility aids in planning
Identify accessible evacuation routes and shelters in advance
Register with local registries for people needing evacuation assistance, if available
Ensure caregivers and neighbors know the specific needs involved
practice_activities: Review the emergency plan specifically for any family members with special needs

quiz.q: Why should evacuation routes be reviewed for accessibility?
quiz.a: Standard routes or shelters may not accommodate mobility or medical needs

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Contact local emergency management for registries or resources supporting people with disabilities.

emergency_preparedness.name: Workplace Emergency Action Plans
learning_objectives: Learn the components of a workplace emergency action plan
Understand employee responsibilities during workplace emergencies
key_steps: Know your workplace's evacuation routes and assembly points
Understand designated roles, such as floor wardens, if assigned
Participate in scheduled workplace emergency drills
Report unclear or missing safety information to management
practice_activities: Locate your workplace's posted emergency action plan and assembly point

quiz.q: What is one component of a workplace emergency action plan?
quiz.a: Designated evacuation routes and an outdoor assembly point

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Workplace emergency plans should follow local occupational safety regulations.

emergency_preparedness.name: Community Disaster Volunteer Basics
learning_objectives: Learn how community members can support disaster response
Understand basic volunteer safety and training options
key_steps: Consider joining a local community emergency response team program
Get trained in basic first aid and CPR before volunteering
Follow the direction of official emergency management during a response
Avoid self-deploying to disaster areas without coordination
practice_activities: Look up local volunteer emergency response training programs

quiz.q: Why should volunteers avoid self-deploying to a disaster area?
quiz.a: Uncoordinated volunteers can strain resources and create additional risks

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Register with recognized volunteer organizations for proper training and coordination.

emergency_preparedness.name: Long-Term Food and Water Storage Planning
learning_objectives: Learn how to plan food and water storage for extended emergencies
Understand rotation and storage best practices
key_steps: Store at least two weeks of food and water per household member
Choose foods with long shelf lives and rotate stock regularly
Store water in food-grade containers away from sunlight
Label supplies with purchase or expiration dates
practice_activities: Calculate your household's two-week food and water storage needs

quiz.q: How much food and water should a household aim to store for emergencies?
quiz.a: At least a two-week supply per person

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Adjust storage recommendations based on local emergency management guidance and household needs.

emergency_preparedness.name: Preparing for Infrastructure Failure (Grid-Down Scenarios)
learning_objectives: Learn how to prepare for extended loss of power and utilities
Understand key backup systems and skills needed
key_steps: Maintain backup power options like batteries, solar chargers, or a generator
Store manual tools that do not require electricity
Keep a supply of cash, as electronic payment systems may be unavailable
Build practical skills like manual water purification and basic repairs
practice_activities: Test the household's backup power sources and manual tools

quiz.q: Why is cash useful during an extended grid-down scenario?
quiz.a: Electronic payment systems may not function without power or network access

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Grid-down preparedness should complement, not replace, official emergency guidance.

emergency_preparedness.name: After-Action Review: Learning From Emergency Events
learning_objectives: Learn how to review and improve after an emergency event
Understand the value of updating plans based on experience
key_steps: Discuss what worked well and what did not after any emergency
Update the family or workplace emergency plan based on lessons learned
Replenish and adjust emergency kits based on actual needs experienced
Share lessons learned with neighbors or community groups
practice_activities: Hold a short family debrief after any emergency drill or real event

quiz.q: Why is an after-action review useful following an emergency?
quiz.a: It helps identify what worked and improve future preparedness plans

emergency_preparedness.important_note: Regularly updating plans based on real experience improves future emergency readiness.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Basic Map Reading
learning_objectives: Read a simple map key
Find north using a map and compass
Plot a route between two points
key_steps: Identify map symbols: scale, contour lines, north arrow
Practice locating landmarks on a local map
Use grid references to find a location
Plan a simple route between two points
practice_activities: Use a local park map to plan a walk
Identify 5 landmarks on a printed map

quiz.q: What does the scale on a map show?
quiz.a: The ratio between distance on the map and real-world distance

quiz.q: What is a grid reference?
quiz.a: A number pair used to identify an exact location on a map

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Always tell a trusted adult your planned route before going outdoors.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Using a Compass
learning_objectives: Identify the four cardinal directions
Take a bearing with a compass
Follow a compass bearing to a destination
key_steps: Hold compass flat and level
Let needle settle and point to magnetic north
Rotate the compass housing to set a bearing
Walk in the direction the arrow points
Adjust for magnetic declination if needed
practice_activities: Practise finding north in the schoolyard
Walk a 4-point compass course around the playground

quiz.q: What do the four cardinal points stand for?
quiz.a: North, South, East, West

quiz.q: What does the red needle on a compass always point to?
quiz.a: Magnetic north

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Always use a compass with adult supervision in unfamiliar outdoor areas.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Weather Awareness
learning_objectives: Read basic weather signs in nature
Understand cloud types and what they predict
Plan outdoor activities safely around weather
key_steps: Cumulus clouds = fair weather; cumulonimbus = thunderstorm approaching
Red sky at night = fair tomorrow; red sky in morning = weather warning
Wind direction changes can signal incoming storms
Check a reliable weather app before outdoor plans
practice_activities: Observe and sketch the clouds each day for a week
Compare predictions to actual weather

quiz.q: What do dark cumulonimbus clouds indicate?
quiz.a: Thunderstorm approaching

quiz.q: What does a red sky in the morning indicate?
quiz.a: Possible bad weather ahead (sailor's warning)

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Weather forecasting apps are your best tool — always check before outdoor activities.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Safe Hiking Basics
learning_objectives: Plan a safe day hike
Pack essential items
Follow trail safety rules
key_steps: Always hike with a group and tell an adult your route
Pack: water, snacks, first aid, sunscreen, torch, map
Stay on marked trails
Turn around if the weather changes or you feel uncertain
Leave no trace: take litter home
practice_activities: Plan a hypothetical day hike using a trail map
Pack a trial hiking day bag at home

quiz.q: Name three things to pack for a day hike.
quiz.a: Water, snacks, first aid kit, sunscreen, map, torch (any three)

quiz.q: What should you do if the weather changes on a hike?
quiz.a: Turn around and return to safety immediately

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Always hike with a responsible adult and inform others of your planned route.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Camping Basics
learning_objectives: Set up a simple tent
Stay safe and warm overnight outdoors
Follow campsite rules and leave no trace
key_steps: Choose a flat, sheltered campsite away from water
Set up tent: insert poles, clip on body, peg out guy ropes
Sleep in layers: moisture-wicking base, warm mid, wind-resistant shell
Keep food sealed to avoid attracting wildlife
Leave no trace: bury waste, pack litter
practice_activities: Set up a tent in the garden with adult supervision
Practise packing a camping bag with the right layers

quiz.q: Where should you not set up a tent?
quiz.a: In a low-lying area prone to flooding or under dead trees

quiz.q: Why seal food when camping?
quiz.a: To avoid attracting animals to your campsite

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Always camp with experienced adults and inform others of your location.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Wildlife Awareness
learning_objectives: Identify common local wildlife
Know safe distances from wild animals
Respond calmly to wildlife encounters
key_steps: Observe wildlife from a distance — never feed wild animals
Make noise on trails to avoid surprising animals
If confronted by a large animal: stay calm, back away slowly, do not run
Recognise local hazardous plants and insects
Never handle an unknown animal — even if it appears tame
practice_activities: Research local wildlife that live in your region
Visit a nature park and practise identifying animals from a distance

quiz.q: What should you do if you encounter a large wild animal?
quiz.a: Stay calm, back away slowly, do not run or make sudden movements

quiz.q: Why should you never feed wild animals?
quiz.a: It makes them dependent on humans and can make them aggressive

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Enjoy wildlife from a respectful distance — do not disturb natural behaviours.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Basic Rope Knots
learning_objectives: Tie three essential knots correctly
Know what each knot is used for
Untie knots safely
key_steps: Square knot: joining two ropes of equal thickness
Bowline: making a fixed loop
Cleat hitch: securing a rope to a post
Practise each knot until fluent from memory
practice_activities: Practise each knot 5 times until you can tie them without instructions
Use rope to practise hanging a simple tarp shelter

quiz.q: What is a bowline knot used for?
quiz.a: Making a fixed loop that does not slip

quiz.q: What is a square knot used for?
quiz.a: Joining two ropes of equal thickness together

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Practise knots with adult supervision — rope safety is important.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Learning the Four Cardinal Directions
learning_objectives: Learn the four cardinal directions
Understand how directions relate to everyday landmarks
key_steps: Learn that a compass rose shows north, south, east, and west
Practice using the sun's rising and setting to estimate east and west
Point out the four directions using familiar landmarks
Use simple direction words when describing where things are
practice_activities: Draw a compass rose and label the four directions

quiz.q: Which direction does the sun rise from?
quiz.a: The east

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Learning directions is a foundational skill before using a compass or map.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Understanding Trail Markers and Signs
learning_objectives: Recognize common trail markers and signs
Understand why trails are marked
key_steps: Look for painted blazes or markers on trees and posts
Follow marked trails and never leave the path without an adult
Recognize signs for danger, closed trails, or points of interest
Tell an adult if a trail marker seems missing or confusing
practice_activities: Spot and count trail markers during a family walk

quiz.q: What should you do if a trail marker seems missing?
quiz.a: Tell an adult right away and do not continue guessing

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Children should always hike on marked trails with adult supervision.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Dressing for Outdoor Weather
learning_objectives: Learn to choose clothing for different weather
Understand the basics of layering
key_steps: Check the weather forecast before heading outside
Wear layers that can be added or removed as needed
Choose sturdy shoes appropriate for the terrain
Bring a hat and rain gear when weather may change
practice_activities: Pack a weather-appropriate outfit for a pretend hike

quiz.q: Why is layering clothing helpful outdoors?
quiz.a: It lets you add or remove clothes as the temperature changes

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: An adult should help young children choose appropriate outdoor clothing.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Staying With Your Group Outdoors
learning_objectives: Understand the importance of staying with a group
Know what to do if separated outdoors
key_steps: Always stay within sight of an adult or group leader
Use the buddy system when exploring
Stop immediately and call out if you notice you are alone
Stay in one place and wait if truly lost
practice_activities: Practice a buddy check-in during an outdoor outing

quiz.q: What should you do first if you realize you are separated from your group?
quiz.a: Stop, stay calm, and call out or wait in place

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Adults should establish clear group rules before any outdoor outing with children.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Basic Nature Observation Safety
learning_objectives: Learn to observe nature safely without touching everything
Understand basic outdoor courtesy
key_steps: Look at plants, insects, and animals without touching them
Ask an adult before picking up anything outdoors
Stay on trails to avoid damaging plants
Keep a respectful distance from wildlife
practice_activities: Keep a simple nature observation list during a walk

quiz.q: Why should children ask before touching plants or animals outdoors?
quiz.a: Some can be harmful, and touching can also hurt wildlife or plants

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Adult supervision helps children learn safe boundaries with nature.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: What to Do If You Get Lost Outdoors
learning_objectives: Learn the basic 'hug a tree' stay-put strategy
Understand how to signal for help if lost
key_steps: Stop moving and stay in one place
Hug a tree or stay near a landmark so you are easier to find
Blow a whistle three times if you have one
Answer loudly if you hear someone calling your name
practice_activities: Practice the 'stop and stay put' response in a pretend lost scenario

quiz.q: What is the first thing to do if you realize you are lost outdoors?
quiz.a: Stop moving and stay in one place

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Teach children this rule before any outdoor activity away from direct supervision.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Sun Safety While Outdoors
learning_objectives: Learn how to protect skin and eyes from the sun
Understand signs of too much sun exposure
key_steps: Apply sunscreen before going outside and reapply regularly
Wear a hat and sunglasses on sunny days
Take breaks in the shade during peak sun hours
Drink water regularly to stay hydrated in the sun
practice_activities: Practice applying sunscreen correctly with an adult's help

quiz.q: What are two ways to protect yourself from the sun outdoors?
quiz.a: Wearing sunscreen and a hat, and taking shade breaks

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Adults should help apply sunscreen and monitor sun exposure for young children.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Recognizing Safe vs Unsafe Terrain
learning_objectives: Learn to identify uneven or risky ground
Understand why to avoid certain terrain
key_steps: Watch for loose rocks, roots, and slippery areas
Walk slowly and carefully on uneven ground
Avoid climbing on unstable rocks or ledges
Ask an adult before crossing streams or unfamiliar terrain
practice_activities: Point out examples of safe and unsafe footing during a walk

quiz.q: What should you do before crossing a stream on a hike?
quiz.a: Ask an adult for help and permission first

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Adults should assess terrain safety before allowing children to explore independently.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Packing a Simple Day Trip Bag
learning_objectives: Learn the basic items needed for a short outdoor trip
Understand why preparation matters
key_steps: Pack water and a snack for the trip
Include a small first aid item and a whistle
Bring a light jacket in case weather changes
Check the bag with an adult before leaving
practice_activities: Pack a sample day bag together with a parent

quiz.q: What are two important items to pack for a short outdoor trip?
quiz.a: Water and a snack

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: An adult should review and help pack a child's outdoor bag.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Identifying Common Trail Hazards
learning_objectives: Learn to recognize common outdoor hazards
Understand how to avoid or report them
key_steps: Watch for roots, rocks, and holes on the trail
Avoid touching unfamiliar plants or mushrooms
Stay away from the edges of cliffs or steep drops
Tell an adult about any hazard you notice
practice_activities: Play a hazard spotting game on a family walk

quiz.q: What should you do if you see an unfamiliar plant on a trail?
quiz.a: Do not touch it and tell an adult

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Adult supervision is essential for identifying and avoiding trail hazards with children.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Introduction to Topographic Maps
learning_objectives: Learn what a topographic map shows
Understand basic map symbols
key_steps: Identify contour lines, trails, and water features on a topo map
Learn common map symbols like campsites and peaks
Compare the map to visible landmarks outdoors
Practice orienting the map using a compass or landmarks
practice_activities: Study a sample topographic map and identify three features

quiz.q: What do contour lines on a topographic map represent?
quiz.a: Elevation and the shape of the land

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Practice topographic map reading with an experienced adult before relying on it outdoors.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Understanding Map Scale and Legends
learning_objectives: Learn how map scale relates to real distance
Understand how to read a map legend
key_steps: Find the scale bar and use it to estimate real distances
Review the legend to understand symbols used on the map
Practice measuring a trail distance using the scale
Compare paper map distances to known trail lengths
practice_activities: Measure the distance between two points on a sample map using the scale

quiz.q: What does a map's scale help you calculate?
quiz.a: The real-world distance between points on the map

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Map reading skills should be practiced with adult guidance before backcountry use.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Using a GPS Device Basics
learning_objectives: Learn how a handheld or phone GPS device works
Understand its benefits and limitations outdoors
key_steps: Mark a starting waypoint before beginning a hike
Learn to read coordinates and follow a route on the device
Carry a paper map and compass as backup, since batteries can fail
Keep the device charged and protected from moisture
practice_activities: Practice marking and navigating to a waypoint in a familiar area

quiz.q: Why should hikers carry a map and compass even when using a GPS device?
quiz.a: GPS devices can lose battery or signal, so a backup is needed

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: GPS devices are helpful tools but should never fully replace map and compass skills.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Finding North Using the Sun
learning_objectives: Learn a simple method to estimate direction using the sun
Understand the shadow-stick method
key_steps: Place a stick upright in the ground and mark the tip of its shadow
Wait about 15 minutes and mark the new shadow tip
Draw a line between the two marks; it runs roughly east-west
Stand with the first mark on your left to face roughly north
practice_activities: Practice the shadow-stick method on a sunny day with an adult

quiz.q: In the shadow-stick method, what direction does the line between the two marks roughly indicate?
quiz.a: East-west

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Sun-based direction finding is an estimate and should be combined with other navigation tools when possible.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Finding North Using the Big Dipper and Polaris
learning_objectives: Learn to locate Polaris, the North Star
Understand how it can be used for direction at night
key_steps: Find the Big Dipper constellation in the night sky
Trace a line from the two outer stars of its bowl
Follow that line to the bright star Polaris
Polaris sits roughly above true north
practice_activities: Practice locating the Big Dipper and Polaris on a clear night with an adult

quiz.q: Which constellation helps you locate Polaris, the North Star?
quiz.a: The Big Dipper

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Night sky navigation should be practiced with an adult in a safe, familiar outdoor location.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Building a Simple Wilderness Shelter
learning_objectives: Learn the basic purpose and structure of an emergency shelter
Understand what materials to use
key_steps: Choose a dry, flat site away from hazards like dead branches
Use a tarp, branches, or natural materials to build a simple lean-to
Insulate the ground with leaves or brush to stay warm
Keep the shelter small to retain body heat
practice_activities: Practice building a simple lean-to shelter with adult supervision

quiz.q: Why is it important to insulate the ground inside a shelter?
quiz.a: The ground can draw away body heat, so insulation helps retain warmth

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Shelter building should be practiced with an experienced adult before relying on it in a real emergency.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Fire Safety Basics: Starting a Fire with Matches
learning_objectives: Learn safe steps for starting a small fire with matches
Understand fire safety precautions
key_steps: Choose a cleared, safe fire spot away from overhanging branches
Gather tinder, kindling, and fuel wood before lighting
Strike the match away from your body and light the tinder carefully
Keep water or dirt nearby to fully extinguish the fire when done
practice_activities: Watch and assist an adult safely build and extinguish a campfire

quiz.q: What should always be kept nearby when starting a fire?
quiz.a: Water or dirt to extinguish it

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Fire starting must always be supervised by a responsible adult and follow local fire regulations.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Water Purification by Boiling
learning_objectives: Learn why wilderness water must be treated before drinking
Understand the boiling method for purification
key_steps: Collect the clearest water available from a moving source if possible
Bring the water to a rolling boil for at least one minute
Boil longer at higher elevations for added safety
Let the water cool before drinking
practice_activities: Watch an adult demonstrate boiling water for purification during a camping trip

quiz.q: How long should water be boiled to help make it safe to drink?
quiz.a: At least one minute, longer at high altitude

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Boiling water requires adult supervision due to the risk of burns and open flame.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Identifying Animal Tracks
learning_objectives: Learn to recognize common animal tracks
Understand what tracks can tell you about nearby wildlife
key_steps: Look for track shape, size, and number of toes
Note the pattern and spacing between tracks
Compare tracks to a field guide or reference chart
Observe tracks from a safe distance without disturbing them
practice_activities: Sketch or photograph animal tracks found on a nature walk

quiz.q: What details help identify an animal track?
quiz.a: Shape, size, number of toes, and spacing pattern

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Never approach the animal that may have made a track; observe signs of wildlife from a safe distance.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Leave No Trace Principles
learning_objectives: Learn the core Leave No Trace principles
Understand why minimizing outdoor impact matters
key_steps: Pack out all trash, including food scraps
Stay on designated trails and campsites
Respect wildlife by observing from a distance
Leave natural objects and historical items as you found them
practice_activities: Practice packing out all trash after an outdoor outing

quiz.q: What is one core Leave No Trace principle?
quiz.a: Pack out everything you pack in, including trash

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Following Leave No Trace principles helps protect natural areas for future visitors.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Basic Outdoor First Aid Kit Use
learning_objectives: Learn the essential contents of an outdoor first aid kit
Understand how to use basic items for minor injuries
key_steps: Check the kit for bandages, gauze, tape, and antiseptic wipes
Clean a minor scrape before applying a bandage
Use blister pads or moleskin for hot spots on feet
Tell an adult immediately about any injury needing more than basic care
practice_activities: Practice using a first aid kit on a pretend scrape with adult guidance

quiz.q: What should be done to a minor scrape before bandaging it?
quiz.a: Clean it first

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Outdoor first aid should be supervised by an adult trained in basic first aid.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Trail Marking and Staying Found
learning_objectives: Learn simple methods to mark a route or stay oriented
Understand how to avoid becoming lost
key_steps: Note landmarks and trail junctions as you pass them
Look back occasionally to see how the trail appears when returning
Use small, temporary markers when permitted, and remove them after
Check a map or GPS regularly rather than only at the end
practice_activities: Practice noting three landmarks during a hike and recalling them afterward

quiz.q: Why is it helpful to look back at the trail while hiking forward?
quiz.a: It helps you recognize the trail when walking back the same way

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Combine trail awareness with a map and compass rather than relying on memory alone.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Recognizing Poisonous vs Safe-Looking Plants
learning_objectives: Understand that many plants can look similar but be harmful
Learn the general rule of caution around unfamiliar plants
key_steps: Never eat, taste, or touch an unfamiliar wild plant
Learn to recognize a few common harmful plants in your region with an adult
Wash skin promptly if it contacts a suspicious plant
Ask a knowledgeable adult or guide before assuming any plant is safe
practice_activities: Review a regional guide to locally harmful plants with an adult

quiz.q: What is the safest rule when encountering an unfamiliar wild plant?
quiz.a: Never touch, taste, or eat it

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Plant identification varies greatly by region; consult a local expert guide rather than relying on assumptions.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Preventing Sunburn and Heat Exhaustion Outdoors
learning_objectives: Learn how to prevent overheating during outdoor activity
Recognize early signs of heat-related illness
key_steps: Drink water regularly, even before feeling thirsty
Take breaks in shade during hot weather
Wear light-colored, breathable clothing and a hat
Stop activity and cool down if feeling dizzy, weak, or overly hot
practice_activities: Practice a hydration schedule during a warm-weather outdoor activity

quiz.q: What is an early sign of heat exhaustion?
quiz.a: Feeling dizzy, weak, or overly hot and tired

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Seek shade, water, and medical attention promptly for symptoms of heat illness.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Layering Clothing for Cold Weather Hikes
learning_objectives: Learn the three-layer clothing system
Understand how to stay warm and dry outdoors
key_steps: Wear a moisture-wicking base layer next to skin
Add an insulating middle layer like fleece or wool
Top with a waterproof, windproof outer layer
Adjust layers before you get too hot or too cold
practice_activities: Practice choosing appropriate layers for a cold-weather outing

quiz.q: What is the purpose of the base layer in cold-weather clothing?
quiz.a: To wick moisture away from the skin

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Getting wet in cold weather increases the risk of hypothermia, so staying dry is essential.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Dead Reckoning Navigation Basics
learning_objectives: Learn the concept of dead reckoning navigation
Understand how to estimate position using direction and distance
key_steps: Note your starting point, compass heading, and travel speed
Track the time and distance traveled in a straight line
Calculate estimated position based on heading and elapsed distance
Recheck position against landmarks or a map regularly
practice_activities: Practice a short dead reckoning exercise in a familiar open area

quiz.q: What two main factors does dead reckoning navigation rely on?
quiz.a: Direction (heading) and distance traveled

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Dead reckoning works best combined with regular landmark checks and should be practiced with an experienced guide.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Reading Contour Lines on a Topo Map
learning_objectives: Learn to interpret elevation changes from contour lines
Understand how line spacing indicates terrain steepness
key_steps: Note that closely spaced contour lines indicate steep terrain
Widely spaced lines indicate gentler slopes
Identify hills, valleys, and ridges from contour line patterns
Use the contour interval to calculate elevation change
practice_activities: Practice identifying a hill and a valley on a sample topo map

quiz.q: What does closely spaced contour lines indicate about terrain?
quiz.a: Steep terrain

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Contour map reading takes practice; start in familiar terrain before relying on it in the backcountry.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Advanced Compass Navigation (Bearings)
learning_objectives: Learn to take and follow a compass bearing
Understand how to navigate to a specific point using bearings
key_steps: Align the compass baseplate between your position and destination on a map
Rotate the bezel to align orienting lines with map north
Read the bearing where the index line meets the dial
Hold the compass level and walk in the direction the needle points
practice_activities: Practice taking a bearing to a visible landmark and walking it accurately

quiz.q: What is a compass bearing used for?
quiz.a: To determine and follow a precise direction to a destination

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Practice bearing navigation in a familiar, open area before using it in unfamiliar terrain.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Fire Starting with a Ferro Rod
learning_objectives: Learn how a ferrocerium rod creates sparks for fire starting
Understand safe technique and fire preparation
key_steps: Prepare fine, dry tinder before striking the rod
Hold the striker steady and pull the rod back quickly at an angle
Direct sparks onto the tinder bundle
Gently blow or fan the ember once it catches to grow the flame
practice_activities: Practice striking a ferro rod onto safe tinder under adult supervision

quiz.q: What should be prepared before striking a ferro rod?
quiz.a: Fine, dry tinder

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Fire-starting tools should be used only with adult supervision and in permitted, safe locations.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Fire Starting by Friction (Bow Drill Awareness)
learning_objectives: Understand the basic principle of friction fire starting
Learn why this method requires significant skill and practice
key_steps: Learn the basic bow drill components: bow, spindle, fireboard, and handhold
Understand that friction generates heat that creates a hot ember
Recognize that this method takes significant practice to master
Always have a backup fire-starting method ready
practice_activities: Watch an experienced instructor demonstrate the bow drill method

quiz.q: What does the friction in a bow drill method eventually create?
quiz.a: A hot ember that can ignite tinder

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Friction fire starting is an advanced skill best learned from an experienced instructor, with reliable backup methods available.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Water Filtration Methods
learning_objectives: Learn how portable water filters work
Understand when filtration alone is sufficient
key_steps: Choose a filter rated to remove bacteria and protozoa
Pre-filter cloudy water through cloth before using the filter
Follow manufacturer instructions for flow and cleaning
Combine filtration with boiling or chemical treatment if viruses are a concern
practice_activities: Practice using a portable water filter under adult supervision

quiz.q: Why might filtration alone not be enough in some regions?
quiz.a: Some filters do not remove viruses, so added treatment may be needed

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Check filter specifications carefully, since not all filters remove the same range of pathogens.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Water Purification Tablets
learning_objectives: Learn how chemical purification tablets work
Understand correct usage and wait times
key_steps: Read and follow the manufacturer's instructions exactly
Add the correct number of tablets per volume of water
Wait the required time before drinking, often 30 minutes or more
Store tablets in a cool, dry place away from children
practice_activities: Review a sample purification tablet's instructions and required wait time

quiz.q: Why is it important to wait the specified time before drinking treated water?
quiz.a: It gives the chemical time to neutralize harmful organisms

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Some purification tablets are not recommended for certain groups, such as those with thyroid conditions; check labels and consult a doctor if unsure.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Packing a Wilderness Survival Kit
learning_objectives: Learn essential items for a wilderness survival kit
Understand how to organize a kit for quick access
key_steps: Include fire-starting tools, a knife, and cordage
Pack a signaling mirror, whistle, and emergency blanket
Add water purification tools and a basic first aid kit
Keep the kit compact, waterproof, and easily accessible
practice_activities: Assemble a personal wilderness survival kit with an adult

quiz.q: Name two essential categories of items in a wilderness survival kit.
quiz.a: Fire-starting tools and signaling devices, plus water treatment and first aid supplies

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Review and restock a survival kit regularly, and tailor it to the specific environment and trip length.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Signaling for Rescue: Mirror and Whistle
learning_objectives: Learn how to use a signal mirror effectively
Understand whistle signaling patterns
key_steps: Aim a signal mirror by sighting through its aiming hole toward aircraft or search parties
Flash the mirror in short bursts to attract attention
Use three whistle blasts as the universal distress signal
Repeat signals periodically and stay in an open, visible area
practice_activities: Practice aiming a signal mirror at a distant object in daylight

quiz.q: What is the universal number of signals used to indicate distress?
quiz.a: Three (three whistle blasts, three flashes, three of anything)

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Signaling tools work best combined with staying in one visible location rather than wandering.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Signaling for Rescue: Ground-to-Air Signals
learning_objectives: Learn basic ground-to-air signal symbols
Understand how to make signals visible from above
key_steps: Use contrasting materials like rocks, logs, or clothing to form large symbols
Make an X shape to signal 'need medical assistance'
Make a V shape to signal 'need assistance'
Build signals in open areas visible from the air, such as clearings or ridgelines
practice_activities: Practice laying out a large signal symbol using available materials

quiz.q: What does a large X symbol signal to rescuers from the air?
quiz.a: That medical assistance is needed

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Ground-to-air signals should be large, high-contrast, and placed in open, visible areas.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Backcountry Trip Planning Basics
learning_objectives: Learn the key steps in planning a safe backcountry trip
Understand the importance of sharing plans with others
key_steps: Research the route, terrain, and weather forecast in advance
Leave a detailed trip plan with a trusted contact, including return time
Check required permits and pack appropriate gear
Build in extra time and a turnaround plan for changing conditions
practice_activities: Draft a sample trip plan including route, timing, and emergency contacts

quiz.q: Why should a trip plan be left with a trusted contact?
quiz.a: So someone knows where to look if you do not return as expected

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Always share detailed trip plans before heading into the backcountry, especially for solo trips.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: River and Stream Crossing Safety
learning_objectives: Learn safe techniques for crossing moving water
Understand when a crossing should be avoided
key_steps: Scout upstream and downstream for a safer, shallower crossing point
Unbuckle backpack straps before crossing in case you need to shed the pack
Face upstream and move sideways using trekking poles for stability
Turn back if the water is too fast, deep, or cold to cross safely
practice_activities: Practice safe crossing stance and pole use in shallow, calm water with an adult

quiz.q: Why should backpack straps be unbuckled before a water crossing?
quiz.a: So the pack can be quickly removed if you fall in

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Water crossings can be extremely dangerous; only attempt them with an experienced adult and turn back if conditions seem unsafe.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Snake and Wildlife Encounter Safety
learning_objectives: Learn safe behavior around wild animals and snakes
Understand how to respond to an encounter
key_steps: Stay alert and watch the trail and surroundings while hiking
Give wildlife plenty of space and never approach or feed animals
Back away slowly if you encounter a snake; do not try to handle it
Know basic signs of a venomous snakebite and seek medical help immediately if bitten
practice_activities: Review common wildlife encounter guidance for your hiking region

quiz.q: What should you do if you see a snake on the trail?
quiz.a: Back away slowly and give it space; do not try to touch or handle it

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Seek immediate medical attention for any snakebite; do not attempt home remedies like cutting or suction.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Recognizing and Preventing Hypothermia
learning_objectives: Learn the causes and warning signs of hypothermia
Understand steps to prevent and respond to it
key_steps: Recognize early signs like shivering, confusion, and fumbling hands
Keep clothing dry and add insulating layers before feeling cold
Get an affected person out of wet clothes and into warm, dry shelter
Seek emergency medical help for severe hypothermia symptoms
practice_activities: Review a checklist of hypothermia warning signs with an adult before a cold-weather trip

quiz.q: What is an early warning sign of hypothermia?
quiz.a: Uncontrollable shivering and confusion

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Hypothermia can be life-threatening; treat early signs seriously and seek medical help for severe cases.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Recognizing and Preventing Heat-Related Illness
learning_objectives: Learn the difference between heat exhaustion and heatstroke
Understand prevention and response steps
key_steps: Recognize heat exhaustion signs like heavy sweating, weakness, and nausea
Recognize heatstroke signs like confusion, hot dry skin, and loss of consciousness
Move to shade, cool the body, and hydrate for heat exhaustion
Call emergency services immediately for suspected heatstroke
practice_activities: Compare heat exhaustion and heatstroke symptoms using a reference chart

quiz.q: What is a key difference between heat exhaustion and heatstroke?
quiz.a: Heatstroke involves confusion and very hot skin and is a medical emergency

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Heatstroke is a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate medical attention.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Basic Orienteering with Map and Compass
learning_objectives: Learn to combine map and compass skills for orienteering
Practice navigating between multiple points
key_steps: Orient the map to match the terrain using the compass
Plot a route between checkpoints using bearings
Pace count or time your travel to estimate distance covered
Recheck your position at each checkpoint before continuing
practice_activities: Complete a simple orienteering course with marked checkpoints

quiz.q: What does it mean to 'orient' a map?
quiz.a: To align the map so its features match the actual terrain direction

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Orienteering courses are a good way to safely practice navigation skills in a controlled setting.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Night Navigation Basics
learning_objectives: Learn the added challenges of navigating at night
Understand tools and techniques for safe night travel
key_steps: Use a reliable headlamp with spare batteries
Rely more heavily on compass bearings since landmarks are harder to see
Move slower and more carefully due to reduced visibility
Avoid night travel in unfamiliar or hazardous terrain when possible
practice_activities: Practice using a headlamp and compass together in a safe, familiar area at dusk

quiz.q: Why is navigation more difficult at night?
quiz.a: Landmarks and terrain features are much harder to see

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Night navigation should only be attempted by experienced individuals with proper equipment and, ideally, adult guidance for teens.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Foraging Safety Awareness
learning_objectives: Understand the risks of foraging without expert knowledge
Learn the general caution rules around wild food
key_steps: Never eat any wild plant, berry, or mushroom without expert identification
Learn from a qualified local expert or guide before ever foraging
Understand that look-alike species can be seriously toxic
When in doubt, do not eat it
practice_activities: Attend or watch a guided foraging walk led by a qualified expert

quiz.q: What is the safest rule if you are unsure whether a wild plant is edible?
quiz.a: Do not eat it

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Foraging safety varies greatly by region and species; always learn from a qualified local expert, never from assumptions.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Building a Debris Hut Shelter
learning_objectives: Learn the structure of a debris hut for insulation
Understand why insulation matters as much as a roof
key_steps: Build a simple ridge pole frame against a support like a fallen log
Add ribbing branches along both sides of the ridge pole
Pile natural debris like leaves and branches thickly over the frame
Fill the inside with dry leaves for insulation, leaving just enough room to fit inside
practice_activities: Practice building a small-scale debris hut frame with adult supervision

quiz.q: Why is a thick layer of debris insulation important on a debris hut?
quiz.a: It traps body heat and keeps the occupant warm

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Shelter-building skills should be practiced with an experienced instructor before relying on them in an emergency.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Layering and Insulation for Winter Camping
learning_objectives: Learn advanced cold-weather clothing and sleep system planning
Understand how to prevent heat loss while camping in winter
key_steps: Use a sleeping bag rated well below expected overnight temperatures
Add an insulating sleeping pad to prevent heat loss to the ground
Keep a dry set of clothes reserved only for sleeping
Avoid overheating and sweating during the day, which can lead to dampness and cold later
practice_activities: Review a winter camping gear checklist with an experienced adult

quiz.q: Why is a sleeping pad important in winter camping?
quiz.a: It insulates against heat loss to the cold ground

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Winter camping carries serious cold-weather risks and should be attempted only with proper training and experienced companions.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Altitude Sickness Awareness
learning_objectives: Learn the causes and symptoms of altitude sickness
Understand prevention and response strategies
key_steps: Ascend gradually and allow time to acclimatize at high elevations
Recognize symptoms like headache, nausea, and fatigue
Stop ascending and rest if mild symptoms appear
Descend immediately if symptoms worsen or become severe
practice_activities: Research the elevation profile and acclimatization plan for an upcoming high-altitude trip

quiz.q: What is the recommended response to worsening altitude sickness symptoms?
quiz.a: Descend to a lower elevation immediately

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Severe altitude sickness can be life-threatening; seek medical attention and descend promptly if symptoms are serious.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Advanced Backcountry Route Planning
learning_objectives: Learn advanced considerations for multi-day backcountry routes
Understand risk assessment for remote travel
key_steps: Study detailed maps, weather patterns, and terrain hazards for the full route
Plan water sources, campsites, and bailout points in advance
Assess group skill level against the route's technical difficulty
File a detailed itinerary with a trusted contact and check in as planned
practice_activities: Draft a multi-day route plan including bailout points and water sources

quiz.q: What is a 'bailout point' in backcountry trip planning?
quiz.a: A pre-identified spot where the group can safely exit the route early if needed

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Advanced backcountry travel carries significant risk; build skills gradually and consider professional guides for challenging routes.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Wilderness Navigation Without a Compass
learning_objectives: Learn backup navigation techniques when tools are unavailable
Understand the limitations of natural navigation methods
key_steps: Use natural indicators like sun position and star patterns as a rough guide
Note consistent environmental clues cautiously, since they are not always reliable
Track your route mentally using landmarks and turns
Prioritize finding high ground to get visual bearings when unsure
practice_activities: Practice estimating direction using only natural clues in a familiar, safe area

quiz.q: Why should natural navigation clues like moss growth be used cautiously?
quiz.a: They can be inconsistent and are not always reliable indicators of direction

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Natural navigation methods are backups only; carrying a map, compass, and/or GPS remains the safest primary approach.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Cold-Weather Survival Shelter Building for Adults
learning_objectives: Learn advanced techniques for building survival shelters in snow or extreme cold
Understand ventilation and insulation requirements
key_steps: Choose a site protected from wind, avalanche paths, and falling hazards
Build snow shelters like quinzees or snow trenches with adequate wall thickness
Always include a ventilation hole to prevent carbon dioxide buildup
Insulate the sleeping area off the snow using branches, pads, or packs
practice_activities: Study advanced snow shelter construction techniques from an experienced winter survival instructor

quiz.q: Why must a snow shelter always include a ventilation hole?
quiz.a: To prevent dangerous carbon dioxide buildup inside the sealed shelter

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Snow shelter building is an advanced skill with real risks like suffocation or collapse; learn from a qualified winter survival instructor.

outdoor_and_navigation.name: Advanced Water Crossing Techniques
learning_objectives: Learn group techniques for crossing hazardous water safely
Understand when a crossing should be abandoned
key_steps: Use a mutual support line or human chain technique for group crossings in moderate current
Assign the strongest member to break current flow at the upstream position
Keep pack straps unbuckled and avoid tying into ropes in fast-moving water
Abandon the crossing and seek an alternate route if conditions are too hazardous
practice_activities: Study group water crossing techniques from a wilderness safety course or guide

quiz.q: Why should a rope generally not be tied directly to a person during a river crossing?
quiz.a: Being tied into a rope in fast water can cause drowning if the person is swept off their feet and held under

outdoor_and_navigation.important_note: Water crossings are among the most dangerous backcountry hazards; get trained instruction before attempting group crossing techniques.

health_and_hygiene.name: Handwashing and Hygiene
learning_objectives: Wash hands correctly using 7 steps
Know when to wash hands
Understand how germs spread
key_steps: Wet hands with clean water
Apply soap and lather for 20 seconds
Scrub all surfaces including between fingers and thumbs
Rinse thoroughly
Dry with a clean towel or air dry
Wash before eating, after toilet, after touching animals, after sneezing
practice_activities: Practise 7-step handwashing technique
Time yourself: 20 seconds of scrubbing

quiz.q: How long should you scrub your hands with soap?
quiz.a: At least 20 seconds

quiz.q: Name two times you should wash your hands.
quiz.a: Before eating, after using the toilet, after touching animals, after sneezing (any two)

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Proper handwashing is one of the most effective ways to prevent illness.

health_and_hygiene.name: Food Safety and Storage
learning_objectives: Identify safe food storage temperatures
Recognise signs of spoiled food
Handle raw and cooked food safely
key_steps: Keep fridge below 5°C and freezer below -18°C
Store raw meat on the bottom shelf of the fridge
Never leave cooked food at room temperature for more than 2 hours
Signs of spoilage: mould, unusual smell, slimy texture, swollen packaging
Wash hands and surfaces before and after handling raw meat
practice_activities: Check fridge temperature at home
Identify which items in a fridge are correctly stored

quiz.q: What temperature should a fridge be kept at?
quiz.a: Below 5°C

quiz.q: Name one sign that food may be spoiled.
quiz.a: Mould, unusual smell, slimy texture, or swollen packaging

health_and_hygiene.important_note: When in doubt, throw it out — food poisoning can be very serious.

health_and_hygiene.name: Hygiene in Emergencies
learning_objectives: Maintain hygiene when normal facilities are unavailable
Purify water when clean water is unavailable
Prevent disease spread in emergency conditions
key_steps: Use hand sanitiser if soap and water unavailable
Use wet wipes to clean wounds if running water is not available
Dispose of waste safely away from water sources and sleeping areas
Signal for help rather than trying to find food or water in unknown terrain
Boil water if uncertain about safety (adult required)
practice_activities: Pack a hygiene kit for emergency use (list items with a parent)
Practise waterless handwashing with hand sanitiser

quiz.q: What can you use to clean hands when there is no water?
quiz.a: Alcohol-based hand sanitiser (at least 60% alcohol)

quiz.q: Where should you dispose of waste in an emergency outdoor situation?
quiz.a: At least 60 metres from water sources and sleeping areas

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Good hygiene prevents disease which is a leading cause of harm in emergencies.

health_and_hygiene.name: Insect and Animal Bite Safety
learning_objectives: Identify common dangerous insects and animals in your region
Treat minor insect bites and stings correctly
Know when to seek medical help
key_steps: Bee sting: remove stinger by scraping (not squeezing), wash, apply ice
Mosquito: apply repellent, wear long sleeves at dusk
Tick: use tweezers to remove close to skin, clean area, monitor for rash
Jellyfish: rinse with seawater (not fresh water), apply heat
Seek medical help if: severe swelling, difficulty breathing, unknown bite
practice_activities: Identify local insects that require caution
Practise removing a simulated tick with tweezers

quiz.q: How do you remove a bee stinger?
quiz.a: Scrape it out sideways — do not squeeze it

quiz.q: When must you seek medical help after a bite?
quiz.a: Severe swelling, difficulty breathing, or an unknown bite

health_and_hygiene.important_note: For severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis), call emergency services immediately.

health_and_hygiene.name: Backpack Preparation for Emergencies
learning_objectives: Pack a grab bag for evacuation
Prioritise essential items
Maintain and update the bag regularly
key_steps: Bag: sturdy, comfortable backpack
Water bottle and purification tablets
3 days of non-perishable snacks
Basic first aid kit
Torch and spare batteries
Phone charger (power bank)
Spare clothing and rain cover
Copy of emergency contacts and ID
practice_activities: Pack a real grab bag at home with a parent
Review and update contents every 6 months

quiz.q: What is a 'grab bag'?
quiz.a: A pre-packed backpack containing essentials for emergency evacuation

quiz.q: How often should you update your grab bag?
quiz.a: Every 6 months — check food expiry and battery condition

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Keep your grab bag near the main exit so it is easy to take when leaving quickly.

health_and_hygiene.name: Brushing and Flossing Your Teeth
learning_objectives: Learn proper toothbrushing technique
Understand why daily dental care matters
key_steps: Brush teeth for two minutes, twice a day
Use a pea-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste
Brush all surfaces: front, back, and chewing surfaces
Ask an adult to help with flossing between teeth
practice_activities: Practice a two-minute brushing routine with a timer

quiz.q: How long should you brush your teeth each time?
quiz.a: About two minutes

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Young children should be supervised while brushing to ensure proper technique and avoid swallowing toothpaste.

health_and_hygiene.name: Bathing and Skin Care Basics
learning_objectives: Learn basic bathing and skin care habits
Understand why regular bathing matters
key_steps: Bathe or shower regularly using soap and water
Wash hair with shampoo as needed
Dry off completely, including between toes
Wear clean clothes after bathing
practice_activities: Create a simple bath-time checklist with a parent

quiz.q: Why is it important to dry off completely after bathing?
quiz.a: Staying damp can lead to skin irritation or fungal growth

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Young children should be supervised during bath time for both hygiene and safety.

health_and_hygiene.name: Covering Coughs and Sneezes Properly
learning_objectives: Learn how to cough and sneeze without spreading germs
Understand why this habit protects others
key_steps: Cough or sneeze into your elbow, not your hands
Use a tissue when possible and throw it away immediately
Wash your hands after coughing or sneezing
Turn away from other people when you cough or sneeze
practice_activities: Practice the elbow-cough technique together as a family

quiz.q: Where should you cough or sneeze if you don't have a tissue?
quiz.a: Into your elbow, not your hands

health_and_hygiene.important_note: This simple habit is one of the most effective ways to reduce the spread of germs.

health_and_hygiene.name: Trimming Nails and Nail Hygiene
learning_objectives: Learn why keeping nails clean and trimmed matters
Understand safe nail care habits
key_steps: Keep nails trimmed short to reduce dirt and germs underneath
Wash under nails carefully during handwashing
Avoid biting nails or picking at hangnails
Ask an adult for help trimming nails safely
practice_activities: Have an adult help trim and clean nails as part of a hygiene routine

quiz.q: Why should nails be kept trimmed?
quiz.a: Long nails can trap dirt and germs

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Nail trimming should be done or supervised by an adult to avoid injury.

health_and_hygiene.name: Hair Washing and Care Basics
learning_objectives: Learn basic hair washing habits
Understand how often hair typically needs washing
key_steps: Wet hair thoroughly and apply a small amount of shampoo
Massage the scalp gently while washing
Rinse thoroughly until no shampoo remains
Brush or comb hair gently once dry
practice_activities: Practice a hair-washing routine with a parent's help

quiz.q: What should you do after applying shampoo to your hair?
quiz.a: Rinse it out thoroughly

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Young children should have an adult assist with hair washing to avoid soap in the eyes.

health_and_hygiene.name: Getting Enough Sleep Every Night
learning_objectives: Understand why sleep is important for health
Learn simple habits for a good bedtime routine
key_steps: Go to bed and wake up at consistent times
Follow a calm bedtime routine, such as reading before bed
Avoid screens close to bedtime
Keep the bedroom dark and quiet for sleeping
practice_activities: Create a simple bedtime routine chart with a parent

quiz.q: Why is a consistent bedtime helpful?
quiz.a: It helps the body get enough rest and stay healthy

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Sleep needs vary by age; young children generally need more sleep than adults.

health_and_hygiene.name: Eating a Balanced Plate of Food
learning_objectives: Learn about different food groups
Understand what a balanced meal looks like
key_steps: Include fruits and vegetables at most meals
Choose whole grains when possible
Include a source of protein like beans, eggs, or meat
Limit sugary snacks and drinks
practice_activities: Build a balanced pretend plate using pictures of different foods

quiz.q: What food groups should a balanced plate generally include?
quiz.a: Fruits, vegetables, grains, and protein

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Consult a pediatrician or nutrition guide for specific dietary needs and portion sizes.

health_and_hygiene.name: Drinking Enough Water Every Day
learning_objectives: Understand why water is important for the body
Learn to notice signs of thirst
key_steps: Drink water throughout the day, not just when very thirsty
Carry a water bottle during outdoor play or school
Drink more water during hot weather or exercise
Choose water over sugary drinks most of the time
practice_activities: Track water intake for a day using a simple sticker chart

quiz.q: Why is it important to drink water even before feeling very thirsty?
quiz.a: Thirst is a sign the body is already becoming dehydrated

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Water needs vary by age, activity level, and climate; ask a parent or doctor about specific needs.

health_and_hygiene.name: Keeping Cuts and Scrapes Clean
learning_objectives: Learn the basic steps for caring for a minor cut or scrape
Understand why cleaning a wound matters
key_steps: Tell an adult right away about any cut or scrape
Let an adult rinse the area with clean water
Cover the area with a clean bandage
Watch for signs of infection like redness or swelling
practice_activities: Practice telling an adult about a pretend scrape and getting help

quiz.q: Why should a cut be cleaned before covering it?
quiz.a: To help remove dirt and germs and reduce infection risk

health_and_hygiene.important_note: An adult should always assist with cleaning and bandaging a child's wound.

health_and_hygiene.name: Telling an Adult When You Feel Sick
learning_objectives: Learn to recognize and describe feeling unwell
Understand why telling an adult quickly matters
key_steps: Notice feelings like a tummy ache, fever, or tiredness
Tell a trusted adult as soon as you feel unwell
Describe how and where you feel bad as clearly as possible
Rest and follow the adult's instructions for care
practice_activities: Practice describing how you feel using simple words like 'hot,' 'achy,' or 'tired'

quiz.q: What should you do as soon as you start feeling sick?
quiz.a: Tell a trusted adult right away

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Children should never wait to report feeling unwell, especially with fever, pain, or difficulty breathing.

health_and_hygiene.name: Understanding Dehydration and How to Prevent It
learning_objectives: Learn the signs of dehydration
Understand how to prevent it during play or exercise
key_steps: Drink water regularly throughout the day and during activity
Watch for signs like dark urine, dry mouth, or dizziness
Drink extra water in hot weather or during exercise
Tell an adult if dehydration signs do not improve after drinking water
practice_activities: Track daily water intake for a week using a simple log

quiz.q: What is one sign of dehydration?
quiz.a: Dark-colored urine, dry mouth, or dizziness

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Severe dehydration can be dangerous; seek medical help if symptoms are serious or do not improve.

health_and_hygiene.name: Basic Wound Cleaning and Bandaging
learning_objectives: Learn the steps to properly clean and bandage a minor wound
Understand when a wound needs adult or medical attention
key_steps: Wash your hands before treating any wound
Rinse the wound gently with clean water to remove dirt
Apply an antiseptic if available and cover with a clean bandage
Get adult help immediately for deep cuts, heavy bleeding, or embedded objects
practice_activities: Practice cleaning and bandaging a pretend wound using a first aid kit

quiz.q: What should you do before touching a wound to treat it?
quiz.a: Wash your hands first

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Deep or heavily bleeding wounds require immediate adult and medical attention, not self-treatment.

health_and_hygiene.name: Recognizing Signs of a Minor Illness
learning_objectives: Learn to recognize common signs of feeling unwell
Understand appropriate first responses
key_steps: Notice symptoms like fever, cough, sore throat, or upset stomach
Tell a trusted adult about any symptoms right away
Rest and drink fluids as advised by an adult
Stay home from school or activities if contagious symptoms are present
practice_activities: Make a simple symptom chart to track how you're feeling

quiz.q: Why should you stay home if you have contagious symptoms?
quiz.a: To avoid spreading illness to others

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Consult a doctor for persistent, severe, or worsening symptoms.

health_and_hygiene.name: Sleep Hygiene: Building a Healthy Bedtime Routine
learning_objectives: Understand what sleep hygiene means
Learn habits that support quality sleep
key_steps: Keep a consistent sleep and wake schedule, even on weekends
Avoid screens for at least 30-60 minutes before bed
Keep the bedroom cool, dark, and quiet
Avoid caffeine and heavy meals close to bedtime
practice_activities: Design a personal bedtime routine checklist

quiz.q: Why should screens be avoided before bedtime?
quiz.a: Screen light and stimulation can make it harder to fall asleep

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Sleep needs vary by age; school-age children generally need about 9 to 12 hours of sleep.

health_and_hygiene.name: Nutrition Basics: Understanding Food Groups
learning_objectives: Learn the major food groups and their roles
Understand the concept of a balanced diet
key_steps: Identify the major food groups: fruits, vegetables, grains, protein, and dairy
Understand that different foods provide different nutrients
Aim to include a variety of food groups at meals
Limit highly processed and sugary foods
practice_activities: Plan a balanced sample meal using each food group

quiz.q: Name two food groups that should typically appear in a balanced meal.
quiz.a: Any two of: fruits, vegetables, grains, protein, dairy

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Individual nutrition needs vary; consult a pediatrician or registered dietitian for specific guidance.

health_and_hygiene.name: Hand Sanitizing Without Soap and Water
learning_objectives: Learn when and how to use hand sanitizer effectively
Understand its limitations compared to handwashing
key_steps: Use an alcohol-based hand sanitizer with at least 60% alcohol
Apply enough to cover all surfaces of both hands
Rub hands together until completely dry
Wash with soap and water as soon as possible, especially if hands are visibly dirty
practice_activities: Practice proper hand sanitizer technique, covering all hand surfaces

quiz.q: What alcohol content should a hand sanitizer have to be effective?
quiz.a: At least 60%

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Hand sanitizer is a backup, not a full replacement, for washing with soap and water when available.

health_and_hygiene.name: Recognizing Signs of a Choking Emergency
learning_objectives: Learn to recognize the universal signs of choking
Understand the importance of getting help immediately
key_steps: Watch for hands clutching the throat, the universal choking sign
Notice if someone cannot speak, cough, or breathe
Call for an adult or emergency help immediately
Do not attempt to treat choking yourself; get trained help
practice_activities: Learn the universal choking sign and how to recognize it in others

quiz.q: What is the universal sign someone uses to indicate they are choking?
quiz.a: Clutching their throat with their hands

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Choking is a medical emergency; call for adult help or emergency services immediately and seek certified first aid training.

health_and_hygiene.name: Understanding When to Call for Help in a Medical Emergency
learning_objectives: Learn to recognize signs of a serious medical emergency
Understand how to get help quickly
key_steps: Recognize signs like difficulty breathing, severe bleeding, or unconsciousness
Call local emergency services or get an adult immediately
Stay with the person and follow dispatcher instructions if alone
Keep calm and speak clearly when describing the emergency
practice_activities: Practice describing a pretend emergency situation clearly and calmly

quiz.q: What should you do if someone is unconscious and not breathing normally?
quiz.a: Call emergency services or get an adult immediately

health_and_hygiene.important_note: In a real emergency, always contact emergency services or a trained adult right away.

health_and_hygiene.name: Allergic Reaction Awareness: Recognizing Signs
learning_objectives: Learn to recognize signs of an allergic reaction
Understand the importance of quick adult response
key_steps: Notice signs like hives, swelling, itching, or difficulty breathing
Tell an adult immediately if you or someone else shows these signs
Avoid the suspected allergen right away
Know that severe reactions require emergency medical care
practice_activities: Review common allergy symptoms with a parent or school nurse

quiz.q: What should you do if you notice signs of a severe allergic reaction?
quiz.a: Tell an adult immediately and seek emergency medical care

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis) are medical emergencies requiring immediate care, including epinephrine if prescribed.

health_and_hygiene.name: Building a Personal Hygiene Kit for Travel
learning_objectives: Learn what to include in a personal hygiene kit
Understand why packing hygiene items matters for travel
key_steps: Pack a toothbrush, toothpaste, and travel-size soap
Include hand sanitizer and tissues
Add any personal items like a hairbrush or feminine hygiene products if needed
Check and restock the kit before each trip
practice_activities: Assemble a personal travel hygiene kit with a parent

quiz.q: Name two basic items that belong in a personal hygiene kit.
quiz.a: Any two of: toothbrush, toothpaste, soap, hand sanitizer, tissues

health_and_hygiene.important_note: An adult should help younger children pack and check their hygiene kit before travel.

health_and_hygiene.name: Hygiene Habits While Traveling
learning_objectives: Learn how to maintain hygiene away from home
Understand travel-specific hygiene risks
key_steps: Wash or sanitize hands frequently, especially before eating
Use bottled or treated water for drinking and brushing teeth where tap water is unsafe
Avoid touching your face after touching public surfaces
Pack familiar hygiene products since options may differ while traveling
practice_activities: Create a travel hygiene checklist before a trip

quiz.q: Why might bottled or treated water be recommended while traveling?
quiz.a: Tap water safety can vary by location

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Research water and food safety guidance for your specific travel destination in advance.

health_and_hygiene.name: Recognizing Signs of Heatstroke
learning_objectives: Learn to identify the warning signs of heatstroke
Understand it is a serious medical emergency
key_steps: Notice signs like hot, dry or flushed skin and confusion
Recognize that heatstroke can include a very high body temperature
Get the person to shade or a cool area immediately
Call emergency services right away, as heatstroke is life-threatening
practice_activities: Review heatstroke warning signs using a reference chart with an adult

quiz.q: Is heatstroke a medical emergency?
quiz.a: Yes, it requires immediate emergency medical attention

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Heatstroke can be fatal without prompt treatment; call emergency services immediately if suspected.

health_and_hygiene.name: Recognizing Signs of Hypothermia
learning_objectives: Learn to identify early warning signs of hypothermia
Understand appropriate first response steps
key_steps: Notice signs like intense shivering, slurred speech, or confusion
Get the person into warm, dry clothing and shelter
Warm the body gradually, avoiding very hot water or direct heat sources
Seek emergency medical help for severe symptoms
practice_activities: Review hypothermia warning signs and appropriate response steps with an adult

quiz.q: What is an early sign of hypothermia?
quiz.a: Intense shivering and confusion

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Severe hypothermia is life-threatening and requires immediate emergency medical care.

health_and_hygiene.name: Understanding When to Rest vs Stay Active When Sick
learning_objectives: Learn how to judge activity levels during illness
Understand why rest supports recovery
key_steps: Rest more when experiencing fever, fatigue, or body aches
Avoid strenuous activity until symptoms improve
Stay hydrated and eat light, nutritious foods while recovering
Ask a parent or doctor before returning to normal activity
practice_activities: Create a simple 'rest and recovery' plan for the next time you feel sick

quiz.q: Why is rest important when you are sick?
quiz.a: It allows the body to use its energy to fight illness and recover

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Consult a doctor about returning to activity after any significant illness.

health_and_hygiene.name: Basic Oral Health: Preventing Cavities
learning_objectives: Learn what causes cavities
Understand daily habits that prevent them
key_steps: Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste
Floss daily to remove food between teeth
Limit sugary snacks and drinks
Visit a dentist regularly for checkups and cleanings
practice_activities: Track brushing and flossing habits for a week using a chart

quiz.q: What is one daily habit that helps prevent cavities?
quiz.a: Brushing twice a day with fluoride toothpaste

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Regular dental checkups help catch and prevent problems early.

health_and_hygiene.name: Safe Food Preparation in the Outdoors
learning_objectives: Learn safe food handling practices while camping or traveling
Understand how to avoid foodborne illness outdoors
key_steps: Wash hands or use sanitizer before handling food
Keep raw meat separate from other foods and use separate utensils
Cook food to safe temperatures using a food thermometer when possible
Store perishable food in a cooler with ice or ice packs
practice_activities: Plan a safe meal prep routine for an upcoming camping trip

quiz.q: Why should raw meat be kept separate from other foods outdoors?
quiz.a: To prevent cross-contamination and foodborne illness

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Food safety risks increase outdoors without refrigeration; plan meals and storage carefully.

health_and_hygiene.name: Safe Food Storage While Camping or Traveling
learning_objectives: Learn how to store food safely without a refrigerator
Understand risks of improperly stored food
key_steps: Use a well-insulated cooler with sufficient ice
Store food away from direct sunlight and heat
Discard perishable food that has been above a safe temperature for too long
Store food securely away from wildlife, using bear-proof containers where needed
practice_activities: Pack a cooler correctly for a sample day trip, separating raw and ready-to-eat foods

quiz.q: Why should food be stored away from wildlife while camping?
quiz.a: To prevent dangerous animal encounters and food contamination

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Follow local guidelines for food storage in areas with bears or other wildlife.

health_and_hygiene.name: Managing Minor Illness at Home
learning_objectives: Learn basic self-care steps for common minor illnesses
Understand when home care is appropriate
key_steps: Rest and stay hydrated during a minor cold or stomach bug
Monitor symptoms and temperature regularly
Use age-appropriate over-the-counter remedies only as directed by a caregiver or doctor
Seek medical care if symptoms worsen or do not improve
practice_activities: Create a simple home care checklist for common minor illnesses

quiz.q: What is an important step to monitor during a minor illness at home?
quiz.a: Symptoms and temperature

health_and_hygiene.important_note: Always involve a parent or caregiver in decisions about medication and care for illness.

health_and_hygiene.name: Knowing When to See a Doctor vs Self-Care
learning_objectives: Learn to distinguish minor symptoms from those needing medical care
Understand warning signs that require professional attention
key_steps: Consider self-care for mild symptoms like a minor cold or slight fever
Seek medical attention for high fever, severe pain, or symptoms lasting more than a few days
Seek immediate emergency care for difficulty breathing, severe bleeding, or loss of consciousness
When unsure, contact a doctor or nurse hotline for guidance
practice_activities: Review a simple decision chart for self-care versus doctor visits with a parent

quiz.q: What is a warning sign that requires immediate emergency care?
quiz.a: Difficulty breathing, severe bleeding, or loss of consciousness

health_and_hygiene.important_note: When in doubt about symptom severity, contact a healthcare professional rather than guessing.

health_and_hygiene.name: Introduction to CPR Awareness (Informational)
learning_objectives: Understand the general purpose of CPR
Learn why certified training is necessary before performing it
key_steps: Understand CPR is used when someone is unresponsive and not breathing normally
Know that calling emergency services is always the first step
Understand that hands-only CPR involves chest compressions for adults, per certified training guidelines
Recognize that proper technique and timing must be learned through a certified course, such as Red Cross or American Heart Association training
practice_activities: Research a local certified CPR course for teens or family members

quiz.q: What should always be done first if someone is unresponsive and not breathing?
quiz.a: Call emergency services immediately

health_and_hygiene.important_note: This is informational only; CPR should be learned and practiced through a certified hands-on course, not from written instructions alone.

health_and_hygiene.name: Recognizing and Responding to a Severe Allergic Reaction
learning_objectives: Learn to recognize signs of anaphylaxis
Understand the general emergency response
key_steps: Recognize signs like difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, and hives
Call emergency services immediately for suspected anaphylaxis
If the person has a prescribed epinephrine auto-injector, help them use it or get an adult to help per their emergency plan
Keep the person calm and lying down while waiting for help, unless breathing is easier sitting up
practice_activities: Learn where a family member's epinephrine auto-injector is kept, if applicable, and its basic emergency plan

quiz.q: What is the first step when anaphylaxis is suspected?
quiz.a: Call emergency services immediately
